# Where each AI assistant gets its local business information

> How ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, Copilot, Siri, Alexa, Meta AI and Grok choose which local businesses to recommend.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

By assistant

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Each assistant checks a business against the sources it trusts before naming it. Google's assistants lean on Google's data, Copilot on Bing, and ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude on their own web searches. The shared foundation is consistent facts, strong reviews and outside mentions.

Every assistant finds local businesses a little differently. Some lean on Google's data, some on Bing, some on their own search. The work that gets you recommended is mostly shared, but the priorities change. Pick an assistant to see how it chooses and what to fix first.

[OpenAI

**ChatGPT** Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website.](../ai/chatgpt/index.html)[Google

**Google AI Overviews and AI Mode** Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data.](../ai/google-ai-overviews/index.html)[Google

**Gemini** Gemini can draw on Google Search and Google Maps, so the businesses it recommends usually have complete Google Business Profiles, strong recent reviews and websites that rank for their services.](../ai/gemini/index.html)[Perplexity

**Perplexity** Perplexity searches the web for every answer and shows its sources.](../ai/perplexity/index.html)[Anthropic

**Claude** When Claude searches the web for a local question, it reads and cites public sources: review sites, guides, news and business websites.](../ai/claude/index.html)[Microsoft

**Microsoft Copilot** Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.](../ai/copilot/index.html)[Apple

**Siri and Apple Intelligence** When someone asks Siri for a nearby business, Apple draws on Apple Maps data.](../ai/siri/index.html)[Amazon

**Alexa+** Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web.](../ai/alexa/index.html)[Meta

**Meta AI** Meta AI lives inside Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger and can search the web for local questions.](../ai/meta-ai/index.html)[xAI

**Grok** Grok, xAI's assistant inside X, searches the web and posts on X.](../ai/grok/index.html)

## What every assistant has in common

All of them want to be confident before they name a business. They get that confidence from agreement across sources, which is why the [11 signals](../signals/index.html) apply everywhere. Start with the [complete guide](../guide/index.html), then use the pages above to set priorities for the assistants your customers use.

# How do I get my business recommended by Alexa?

> Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web. Accurate listings on the major directories and review sites, especially the ones that feed voi.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/alexa/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Alexa+

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web. Accurate listings on the major directories and review sites, especially the ones that feed voice assistants, give Alexa the details it needs.

## How does Alexa+ choose which local businesses to recommend?

Amazon's newer Alexa+ assistant handles more conversational requests, including finding and booking local services. It relies on partner data sources and listings rather than one public index, which makes consistent, accurate directory data the priority.

New data from our research team

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks). [Local AI Registry data](../../methodology/index.html)

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**1 of 207** local AI answers gave a street address or phone number](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle)[**83.6%** of local AI answers told people to check with their local store](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle)

**1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number.** Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places.Figure 16, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

**AI answers local questions with national facts.** 65.7% of local answers spoke about “all locations” or “most stores” (vs 2.3% of other answers), and 83.6% hedged (vs 2.6%). National facts are the AI’s default for local questions.Figure 15, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png)

## Do you track Alexa+?

Our monthly check covers ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini today, the assistants most people use to find a local business. Alexa+ isn't in the monthly check yet. The good news: the work that gets you named by one assistant carries over to the others, because they all read the same kinds of sources. A business that's consistent, reviewed and written about is easier for every assistant to recommend.

# How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?

> Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/chatgpt/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

ChatGPT

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website. Then give ChatGPT sources that agree: the same name, address, phone and hours everywhere, steady reviews on more than one site, mentions on local best-of lists and articles, and a clear page for every service.

## How do I claim my business in ChatGPT?

OpenAI opened **Business Hub** in November 2026, a free beta where owners claim the profile ChatGPT already keeps for their business. Open Business Hub from the ChatGPT sidebar, search for your business and claim it. You then confirm you own or represent it through one of the routes offered: your business phone, business email, a DNS record on your website's domain, or a Shopify login. OpenAI also asks for an identity check before you can publish changes or see insights.

Once approved you can update your website, description, category, logo and photos, and see 28 days of insights: how often ChatGPT mentioned you, clicks to your site and the topics people found you through. Local businesses in the US claim an existing listing rather than creating a new one.

OpenAI is clear that claiming does not guarantee better placement. It gives you control of the facts you supply. Our step-by-step guide covers every screen: [how to claim your business in ChatGPT](../../guide/claim-your-business-in-chatgpt/index.html). OpenAI's own help article: [Setting up your business on ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001635-setting-up-your-business-on-chatgpt).

What we saw when we asked ChatGPT ourselves

- In New York, ChatGPT put four different surgeons first across six asks of the same question on Nov 13, 2026.
- After its list, ChatGPT asked follow-up questions: the result the person wants, first surgery or revision, and in one run their budget.
- Most entries quoted a RealSelf rating and review count.

[See every screenshot in AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html)

New data from our research team

**29%**

When ChatGPT got the same local question about 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses it named appeared in both answers (8ight.AI, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**3.5%**

Only 3.5% of businesses ChatGPT named in localized searches appeared at every test point across a town (BrightLocal, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**52.8%**

ChatGPT declined to recommend an orthopedic surgeon in 52.8% of 40,500 persona-based requests (Haupt et al., 2026, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions, and [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html), our screenshots of ChatGPT's answers. Every number links to its chart.

[**2 of 10** US cities got the same #1 surgeon in six ChatGPT asks of one question](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**27 of 30** ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**~35%** of cited sources stayed the same when the same question was worded differently](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording)

**Different wording, different sources, same answer.** Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer.Illustration 5, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

**Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated.Figure 20, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

## Can ChatGPT read my website?

ChatGPT search finds websites with a crawler called **OAI-SearchBot**. OpenAI says sites that block it will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, and that a change to robots.txt takes about 24 hours to apply. Ask whoever runs your website to check that your robots.txt file, firewall and hosting all let it in:

```
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
```

Two other OpenAI crawlers are separate. **GPTBot** collects content that may be used to train OpenAI's models, and you can block it without leaving ChatGPT search. ** ChatGPT-User** visits a page when a person asks ChatGPT to open it. Source: [OpenAI's crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots).

Make sure your pages also load without a login, list your name, address, phone and hours as text (not only in an image), and are in a sitemap.

## How does ChatGPT choose which local businesses to recommend?

For local questions, ChatGPT usually searches the web before answering. It reads a handful of results, including review sites, maps listings, local guides and business websites, then writes a short answer that names a few businesses. When it shows sources, those are the pages that shaped the answer.

OpenAI has not published a full list of the data providers behind its local results, so the practical approach is to be strong in the places it is seen to cite: review platforms, local best-of lists, news and your own site.

## What did ChatGPT say when we asked it 16 local questions?

On Nov 13, 2026 our research team asked ChatGPT 16 local questions, three times each, and screenshotted every answer. The table counts how many different businesses came back across the three asks, and how many were named every single time.

| Question | Different names | Named all 3 times |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “best Botox injector in Newport Beach” | 10 | 0 |
| “best aesthetic clinic in Beaconsfield” | 5 | 3 |
| “best aesthetic clinic in London” | 10 | 1 |
| “best breast augmentation surgeon in NYC” | 7 | 3 |
| “best closed rhinoplasty surgeon in Los Angeles” | 6 | 3 |
| “best lip filler in Newport Beach” | 9 | 1 |
| “best plastic surgeon in New York City” | 12 | 1 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Atlanta” | 7 | 3 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Chicago” | 6 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Dallas” | 7 | 1 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Houston” | 6 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Miami” | 5 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in New York” | 13 | 0 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Phoenix” | 7 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in San Diego” | 6 | 3 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Scottsdale” | 6 | 3 |

Two patterns stand out. In crowded markets like New York, ChatGPT gave a different shortlist almost every time: 13 different names for one rhinoplasty question, and nobody made all three lists. In smaller markets the shortlist was steadier. So being named once proves very little. What matters is how often you're named across many asks, which is exactly what we measure for clients. ## Frequently asked questions

Can I pay ChatGPT to recommend my business?

No. ChatGPT now shows some ads, labeled and kept separate from its answers, and OpenAI says advertising does not influence ChatGPT's own recommendations. Claiming your Business Hub profile is free and does not buy placement either.

Do I have to allow GPTBot to show up in ChatGPT?

No. GPTBot is OpenAI's training crawler. Showing up in ChatGPT search depends on OAI-SearchBot, which you can allow on its own.

Why does ChatGPT give different businesses each time?

Answers vary with wording, location and the sources it happens to read. Businesses that are strong across many sources show up most consistently.

# How do I get my business recommended by Claude?

> When Claude searches the web for a local question, it reads and cites public sources: review sites, guides, news and business websites.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/claude/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Claude

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** When Claude searches the web for a local question, it reads and cites public sources: review sites, guides, news and business websites. Consistent details, strong reviews and independent coverage give it the confidence to name you.

## How does Claude choose which local businesses to recommend?

Claude, made by Anthropic, can search the web when a question needs current information, such as where to find a service nearby, and it cites the pages it used. It tends to favor sources that agree with each other and to be careful about recommending businesses it can't confirm.

New data from our research team

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**63.9%**

Doctors named by AI matched real clinicians 63.9% of the time with web search, compared with 10.8% without it (Ibrahim and Zaki, 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

# How do I get my business to show up in Microsoft Copilot?

> Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/copilot/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Microsoft Copilot

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.

## How does Microsoft Copilot choose which local businesses to recommend?

Copilot is Microsoft's assistant across Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft 365. Its web answers are grounded in Bing search results, which means your Bing presence matters more here than anywhere else.

New data from our research team

# How do I get my business into Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode?

> Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/google-ai-overviews/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Google AI Overviews and AI Mode

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data. A complete, active Google Business Profile, strong reviews, pages that rank for your services and clear structured data on your website are the foundation.

## How does Google AI Overviews and AI Mode choose which local businesses to recommend?

AI Overviews appear above regular Google results, and AI Mode is a full conversational search. For local questions both draw on Google's search index and its local business data, the same information behind Google Maps. Google publishes guidance that the same practices behind good search results apply to its AI features.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**67.5%**

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**76.4%** of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category)[**67.5%** of citations in local AI answers came from news coverage](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration)[**1.0%** of citations went to the business itself for generic “what's open” questions](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap)[**7.2** sources cited per local AI answer, versus 8.1 for other topics](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#sources-per-ai-overview-answer-distribution)

**Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.Figure 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**Local searches got an AI answer 76% of the time, even more often than other questions.** Controlling for phrasing, local searches were still 12 points more likely to get an AI Overview than other question-style searches (76.4% vs 64.1%).Figure 4, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png)

**How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business.** For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store.Illustration 2, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

**The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited.** Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places.Figure 9, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.png)

## What did 7,583 Google AI answers show?

For [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our research team pulled thousands of Google AI answers to local questions and read every source each one cited. Here is what Google's AI did with local businesses:

| Finding | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic | 76.4% |
| Of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites | 6.5% |
| Of citations in local AI answers came from news coverage | 67.5% |
| Of local AI answers told people to check with their local store | 83.6% |
| Local AI answers gave a street address or phone number | 1 of 207 |
| Sources cited per local AI answer, versus 8.1 for other topics | 7.2 |
| Of local AI claims were supported by the pages the AI cited | 87.8% |
| Of business-site citations came from beyond Google's first page | 4.1% |
| More likely: local TV station sites cited in local answers vs other answers | 18x |

Put simply: Google's AI shows up on most local searches, it rarely quotes the business's own website, and it leans on news and other outside sources. It also tells people to check with the store far more often than it gives them an address. The business that wins is the one other sites describe clearly and consistently.

# Local AI search glossary

> Plain-language definitions of GEO, AEO, AI Overviews, entities, schema markup, llms.txt, AI Score and other local AI search terms.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/glossary/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Glossary

Plain definitions of the terms you'll meet when you work on getting your business recommended by AI. Each one says what the term means, why it matters for a local business and what to do about it.

## AEO (answer engine optimization)

**Writing and structuring content so assistants and search features can lift a direct answer from it.**

AEO puts the answer first: a clear two-sentence response to the question, followed by detail, an FAQ and [schema markup](../glossary/index.html#schema-markup). It overlaps with [GEO](../glossary/index.html#geo); AEO is about how your pages are written, GEO is about the wider set of sources AI trusts.

Related: [GEO (generative engine optimization)](../glossary#geo/index.html), [AI Overviews](../glossary#ai-overviews/index.html), [Schema markup](../glossary#schema-markup/index.html)

New data from our research team

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks). [Local AI Registry data](../methodology/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**76.4%** of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category)[**147 vs 70** times a store's own site ranked on page one, vs times the AI cited it, across 157 brand questions](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews)

**SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.** Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links.Illustration 1, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

**One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.Illustration 6, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

## AI Overviews

**The AI-written summaries Google shows above some search results.**

AI Overviews summarize an answer and link to sources. For local questions they draw on Google's search index and local business data. Google's AI Mode is a separate, conversational search built on the same data. See [how to show up in Google's AI answers](../ai/google-ai-overviews/index.html).

Related: [AEO (answer engine optimization)](../glossary#aeo/index.html), [Entity](../glossary#entity/index.html)

## AI Score

**Local AI Registry's measure of how ready a business is to be recommended by AI, based on the 11 signals.**

The AI Score looks at all [11 signals](../signals/index.html) AI uses to decide which local business to recommend and summarizes them in one number, with the detail behind it. Our [free AI visibility check](../tools/ai-visibility-check/index.html) starts with it.

Related: [AI visibility](../glossary#ai-visibility/index.html), [AI share of voice](../glossary#share-of-voice/index.html), [Local AI Blueprint™](../glossary#local-ai-blueprint/index.html)

## AI SEO

**A broad term for search optimization that accounts for AI answers as well as traditional rankings.**

People use AI SEO to mean anything from using AI tools to write content to optimizing for AI assistants. On this site we mean the second: making sure AI assistants recommend your business. See [GEO](../glossary/index.html#geo) and [AEO](../glossary/index.html#aeo).

Related: [GEO (generative engine optimization)](../glossary#geo/index.html), [AEO (answer engine optimization)](../glossary#aeo/index.html)

## AI share of voice

**The share of relevant AI answers that name your business compared with competitors.**

If you ask 20 customer questions across several assistants and you are named in 6 of the answers, that is your share of voice for that question set. Tracking it monthly is the core of [AI monitoring](../signals/ai-monitoring/index.html).

Related: [AI Score](../glossary#ai-score/index.html), [AI visibility](../glossary#ai-visibility/index.html)

## AI visibility

**How often, and how well, AI assistants mention and recommend a business when people ask questions it could answer.**

AI visibility is to assistants what search rankings are to Google. A business with strong AI visibility is named when someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini or Google's AI answers for the kind of service it offers, and it is described accurately. It depends on [eleven signals](../signals/index.html), from [consistent listings](../signals/directory-listings/index.html) to [reviews](../signals/reputation/index.html).

Related: [GEO (generative engine optimization)](../glossary#geo/index.html), [AEO (answer engine optimization)](../glossary#aeo/index.html), [AI Score](../glossary#ai-score/index.html)

## Citation

**A mention of your business on another website, or a source an AI assistant links to in its answer.**

The word has two uses. In local SEO, a citation is any listing or page that mentions your business details. In AI answers, a citation is a source the assistant shows to back up what it said. Being cited by AI usually starts with being cited around the web.

Related: [NAP consistency](../glossary#nap-consistency/index.html), [GEO (generative engine optimization)](../glossary#geo/index.html)

## Entity

**A distinct, identifiable thing, such as a business, person or place, that search engines and AI track as one object with known facts.**

To an assistant, your business is an entity with a name, location, category, services, people and reviews. The clearer and more consistent those facts are across the web, the more confidently AI can talk about you. [Schema markup](../glossary/index.html#schema-markup) and [NAP consistency](../glossary/index.html#nap-consistency) are how you make your entity clear.

Related: [Knowledge graph](../glossary#knowledge-graph/index.html), [NAP consistency](../glossary#nap-consistency/index.html), [Structured data](../glossary#structured-data/index.html)

## GEO (generative engine optimization)

**The practice of improving how a business or brand appears in answers written by AI assistants.**

GEO focuses on the sources AI reads and cites: reviews, articles, lists, structured data and your own pages. For a local business, GEO means making sure every assistant can confirm who you are, what you do and why you're a good choice. See how it compares with traditional SEO in [AI visibility vs SEO](../signals/seo/index.html).

Related: [AEO (answer engine optimization)](../glossary#aeo/index.html), [AI SEO](../glossary#ai-seo/index.html), [Citation](../glossary#citation/index.html)

## Knowledge graph

**A database of entities and how they connect, used by search engines and AI to understand facts.**

Google's Knowledge Graph and similar systems link your business to its location, category, people and other facts. A strong presence in these graphs makes it easier for AI to recognize and describe you.

Related: [Entity](../glossary#entity/index.html), [Structured data](../glossary#structured-data/index.html)

## llms.txt

**A proposed plain-text file at the root of a website that points AI systems to its most useful pages.**

llms.txt is a community proposal, not an official standard, and assistants vary in whether they use it. It's quick to add and does no harm. Make one with our [llms.txt generator](../tools/llms-txt-generator/index.html).

Related: [Structured data](../glossary#structured-data/index.html)

## Local AI Blueprint™

**Local AI Registry's done-for-you program that works all 11 signals for a business.**

The Local AI Blueprint™ is one plan, one team and one monthly report covering every signal AI checks. Learn more on the [Blueprint page](../blueprint/index.html) and about [our 90-day guarantee](../guarantee/index.html).

Related: [AI Score](../glossary#ai-score/index.html), [AI visibility](../glossary#ai-visibility/index.html)

## NAP consistency

**Having the same business name, address and phone number everywhere your business is listed.**

NAP stands for name, address, phone. Many practitioners add hours. Inconsistent NAP makes it harder for AI to confirm which listings belong to you. See [directory listings](../signals/directory-listings/index.html).

Related: [Entity](../glossary#entity/index.html), [Citation](../glossary#citation/index.html)

## Schema markup

**Code added to a web page that labels facts, such as your business name, hours, services and reviews, in a standard vocabulary.**

Schema markup uses the shared vocabulary at schema.org, usually written as JSON-LD. It doesn't change how a page looks; it tells machines exactly what the page is about. Build yours with our free [schema generator](../tools/schema-generator/index.html).

Related: [Structured data](../glossary#structured-data/index.html), [Entity](../glossary#entity/index.html)

## Structured data

**Information organized in a fixed format machines can read without interpretation.**

Schema markup is the most common kind of structured data on websites. Business listings, menus and inventory feeds are others. The more of your key facts exist as structured data, the less AI has to guess.

Related: [Schema markup](../glossary#schema-markup/index.html), [Knowledge graph](../glossary#knowledge-graph/index.html)

# How to get your local business recommended by AI

> How to get your local business recommended by ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI: how assistants decide, the 8 steps in order, and the 11 signals behind every.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/guide/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

The complete guide

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** AI assistants recommend the local businesses they can confirm from many trusted sources. First make sure AI can find you: let OpenAI’s crawler read your site, claim Bing Places and claim your business in ChatGPT. Then make your details identical everywhere, complete your Google profile, build steady reviews, give each service a clear page, get onto the lists and articles AI reads, and check what each assistant says every month.

## How AI decides which local business to recommend

When someone asks ChatGPT "who's the best dentist near me?" or asks Google's AI for a plumber who can come today, the assistant doesn't hold a ranked list of every business. It looks the question up, reads what it can find, and names the few businesses it is most confident about.

Confidence comes from agreement. If your website, your Google profile, three review sites, a local news story and a best-of list all describe the same business at the same address doing the same thing, the assistant can name you without worrying it's wrong. If your details conflict, your reviews are thin and nobody else mentions you, it plays it safe and names someone else.

So the job isn't to trick an algorithm. It's to make your business the easiest one in your area to confirm.

From our AI Answer Watch

- We asked ChatGPT “best rhinoplasty surgeon in [city]” six times in each of 10 US cities on one afternoon, Nov 13, 2026. Only 2 of the 10 cities got the same #1 every time.
- A narrower question gave a steadier answer: for “best closed rhinoplasty surgeon in Los Angeles,” ChatGPT named the same surgeon in all three runs.
- So measure how often AI names you across repeated asks, not where you land in one screenshot.

[See every screenshot in AI Answer Watch](../answer-watch/index.html)

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## Start here: the three steps ChatGPT itself gives

On Nov 13, 2026 we asked ChatGPT "how do I get my local business recommended by ChatGPT?" Its first steps weren't about content or links. They were about making sure it can find and read your business at all. Do these first; each takes minutes.

1. **Let ChatGPT read your website** ChatGPT finds websites with OpenAI's search crawler, called OAI-SearchBot. If your site blocks it, ChatGPT can't cite your pages. Ask whoever runs your site to check the `robots.txt` file allows it:

   ```
   User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
   Allow: /
   ```

   Also check that your hosting or security firewall isn't blocking it. OpenAI lists its crawlers in [its crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots).
2. **Claim your business on Bing Places** Microsoft's Copilot answers from Bing, and ChatGPT tells owners to set up Bing Places alongside Google. It's free at [bingplaces.com](https://www.bingplaces.com/), and you can import your Google profile so the details match exactly.
3. **Claim your business in ChatGPT** OpenAI's Business Hub lets you claim your listing inside ChatGPT, correct your details, get a verified badge and see how often ChatGPT shows you. [Step-by-step: claim your business in ChatGPT](../guide/claim-your-business-in-chatgpt/index.html).

With those done, AI can find you. The eight steps below are what make it choose you.

## The 8 steps, in order

1. **See where you stand** Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google the questions your customers ask, with your city. Write down who is named and which sources each assistant cites. Those sources are your map. The [prompt finder](../tools/prompt-finder/index.html) gives you the questions; a [free check](../tools/ai-visibility-check/index.html) does it with you.
2. **Make your facts identical everywhere** Same name, address, phone and hours on your site, your Google profile and every directory. This is the foundation every other step depends on. [Directory listings guide](../signals/directory-listings/index.html).
3. **Complete and activate your Google profile** Right category, every service, weekly posts, real photos. Google's AI and Gemini read it directly; other assistants see it through search. [Google profile guide](../signals/google-profile/index.html).
4. **Build a steady flow of reviews** Ask every customer, on more than one site, and reply to every review. Reviews that name the service are what AI quotes back. [Reputation guide](../signals/reputation/index.html).
5. **Give each service its own clear page** Answer the question in the first two sentences, add an FAQ and structured data. AI can't recommend you for a service your site barely mentions. [Web management guide](../signals/web-management/index.html) and [SEO guide](../signals/seo/index.html).
6. **Get onto the lists and articles AI reads** The sources the assistants cited in step 1 are your outreach list. [Best-of guides](../signals/best-of-guides/index.html), [third-party articles](../signals/third-party-articles/index.html) and [PR](../signals/pr/index.html).
7. **Add video and labeled photos** Short videos that answer customer questions, and photos named and described for what they show. [Video](../signals/video/index.html) and [photo codifying](../signals/photo-codifying/index.html).
8. **Check every month** AI answers change. Repeat step 1 monthly, compare, and work on whatever the winning businesses have that you don't. [AI monitoring guide](../signals/ai-monitoring/index.html).

Prefer one page you can print? Use [the checklist](../guide/checklist/index.html).

## How it differs by assistant

The foundation is the same everywhere, but each assistant leans on different sources. Google's AI answers and Gemini lean on Google's data. Copilot leans on Bing. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude run their own web searches and cite what they read.

# The AI visibility checklist for local businesses

> A one-page checklist to get your local business recommended by AI: facts, Google profile, reviews, website, outside proof, media and monthly monitoring.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/guide/checklist/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Checklist

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Work through eight areas in order: facts, Google profile, reviews, website, search, outside proof, media and monitoring. Each item below links to a full guide.

Print this page or work through it with your team. Each section links to a full guide.

## Facts

- ☐ Pick one official name, address, phone and hours
- ☐ Update your website, Google profile, Apple Maps and Bing Places
- ☐ Fix or close every other listing that differs

[Full guide](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

New data from our research team

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**83.6%**

83.6% of local AI answers told people to check with their local store, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

# How to claim your business in ChatGPT

> Step by step: how to claim and verify your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub, what it changes, what it doesn't, and five things to check first.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/guide/claim-your-business-in-chatgpt/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

New from OpenAI

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Sign in to ChatGPT, open Business Hub, find your business and verify it by phone, business email, website domain or Shopify. After OpenAI approves the claim, verify your identity with Persona to publish changes, get the blue check and see how often ChatGPT shows you. Claiming is free, but it doesn't guarantee ChatGPT will recommend you.

On November 10, 2026, OpenAI opened Businesses in ChatGPT: a way for owners to claim their business inside ChatGPT, keep its details current and see how often ChatGPT shows it. Here's how to do it, step by step, and what it will and won't change.

## How to claim your business in ChatGPT

1. **Sign in and find your business** Sign in to ChatGPT and open Business Hub from the sidebar (or go to [chatgpt.com/business-hub](https://chatgpt.com/business-hub)). Search for your business by name and pick the listing that matches. Local businesses can currently claim only an existing US listing.
2. **Verify that it's yours** Choose one of the methods offered: a code by text or call to your business phone, a code to your business email, a TXT record added to your website's DNS, or your Shopify store. If someone else manages your domain, ask them to add the record.
3. **Wait for approval** OpenAI reviews the claim and emails you its decision or a request for more information.
4. **Verify your identity with Persona** To publish changes, see insights or get the blue check, you complete identity verification with Persona. Have a government ID, business registration details and proof you can represent the business ready. Make sure the name and address match your official records exactly.
5. **Update your details** Add or correct your website, description, category, logo and cover photo. OpenAI reviews changes before they appear, and ChatGPT can still draw on other sources.
6. **Add your team or agency** The admin who claimed the business can add teammates and grant an agency access. Use each person's own ChatGPT account, and never forward a personal claim invitation.

## What claiming does

- You can correct the details ChatGPT shows about you.
- A blue check appears once your Persona verification is approved.
- You see insights for the last 28 days: mentions, website clicks and the topics where you come up. For a local business, a mention counts when ChatGPT shows a result for your location.

## What it doesn't do

OpenAI is clear that claiming "does not guarantee higher placement or sales," and that ChatGPT keeps making its own recommendations. Advertising doesn't change its answers either. ChatGPT still decides from what it reads about you across the web: your reviews, your listings, articles about you and your own site.

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**67.5%**

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

## Before you claim: five things to check

- **Your name, address and phone match everywhere.** If your website, Google profile and listings disagree, you're handing ChatGPT a conflict. [Why it matters](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html).
- **Your hours are written out as text** on your site, not only in an image.
- **Your site isn't blocking OpenAI's crawler.** OpenAI says sites must allow OAI-SearchBot to appear in ChatGPT search.
- **Your site has LocalBusiness schema.** [Free schema generator](../../tools/schema-generator/index.html).
- **The person claiming can verify.** Whoever controls the business phone, email or domain should do it, or be there when it's done.

## Frequently asked questions

How do I claim my business in ChatGPT?

Sign in to ChatGPT, open Business Hub, search for your business, choose the matching listing and verify by phone, business email, website domain or Shopify. After OpenAI approves the claim, complete identity verification with Persona to publish changes and see insights.

Is claiming my business in ChatGPT free?

Yes. You don't need an Ads account or an Enterprise agreement to claim an eligible business.

Will claiming make ChatGPT recommend my business?

Not by itself. OpenAI says claiming doesn't guarantee higher placement. ChatGPT still recommends based on what it reads about you across the web.

Can my agency manage my ChatGPT business profile?

Yes. The admin who claimed the business can add teammates and grant an agency access in Business Hub.

Can local businesses outside the US claim a listing?

For now, local stores and restaurants can claim only an existing US listing.

# Why doesn't ChatGPT recommend my business?

> The seven most common reasons ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI don't recommend a local business, and how to find and fix yours.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/guide/not-showing-up/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Troubleshooting

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Usually because the assistant can't confirm enough about you, or it can confirm more about a competitor. Conflicting details, thin reviews, unclear service pages and no outside mentions are the most common causes.

## The seven most common reasons

01

**Your details conflict across the web**  
If listings show different phones, addresses or names, AI can't be sure which business is real. [How to fix it](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

02

**Your reviews are thin or old**  
Fewer, older reviews than nearby competitors make you the riskier recommendation. [How to fix it](../../signals/reputation/index.html)

03

**Your site doesn't clearly say what you do**  
If a service has no page of its own, AI has nothing to quote for it. [How to fix it](../../signals/web-management/index.html)

04

**Nobody else talks about you**  
No articles, lists or press means no outside proof. [How to fix it](../../signals/third-party-articles/index.html)

05

**You're missing from the lists AI reads**  
Assistants often answer "best" questions from local best-of lists. [How to fix it](../../signals/best-of-guides/index.html)

06

**Your Google profile is incomplete**  
Google's AI and Gemini lean on it directly. [How to fix it](../../signals/google-profile/index.html)

07

**The question is too far from what you offer**  
AI matches questions to services. If you never mention a service, you won't be named for it. [How to fix it](../../signals/seo/index.html)

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks). [Local AI Registry data](../../methodology/index.html)

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

# The 11 signals AI checks before it recommends a local business

> The eleven signals ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI use to decide which local business to recommend, with a guide to checking and fixing each one.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

The 11 signals

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** AI assistants recommend the local businesses they can confirm from many trusted sources. Those sources fall into eleven signals: listings, press, video, SEO, website, reviews, Google profile, photos, outside articles, best-of lists and monitoring.

When someone asks an AI assistant for a local business, the assistant has to decide which few to name. It decides by checking what it can confirm about each business across the web. We group what it checks into eleven signals. Each one below has its own guide: what it is, how to check yours and how to fix it.

01

**[Directory listings](../signals/directory-listings/index.html)**  
Same name, address, phone and hours everywhere. AI assistants compare what different websites say about your business.

02

**[Press coverage](../signals/pr/index.html)**  
Real news coverage AI can cite. Yes.

03

**[Video](../signals/video/index.html)**  
Explainer videos that answer what customers ask. Video helps in two ways.

04

**[SEO](../signals/seo/index.html)**  
The Google searches you rank for, and should. Yes.

05

**[Website](../signals/web-management/index.html)**  
A fast site with the code AI reads. Your site needs to load fast, work on a phone, state plainly what you do and where, and include structured data (schema) that labels your business, services, hours and reviews in a format machines read without guessing.

06

**[Reviews](../signals/reputation/index.html)**  
Reviews, ratings and replies across sites. Reviews are one of the main things assistants use to decide who to recommend.

07

**[Google profile](../signals/google-profile/index.html)**  
Complete, active and posting every week. Yes, heavily for Google's own AI answers and Gemini, which draw on Google's local data, and indirectly for other assistants that read Google results.

08

**[Photos](../signals/photo-codifying/index.html)**  
Photos labeled so AI can read what they show. Partly.

09

**[Outside articles](../signals/third-party-articles/index.html)**  
Features about you on independent sites. Assistants trust what independent sites say about you more than what you say about yourself.

10

**[Best-of guides](../signals/best-of-guides/index.html)**  
A place on the local best-of lists AI quotes. Often, yes.

11

**[AI monitoring](../signals/ai-monitoring/index.html)**  
What every assistant says about you, each month. Ask it, regularly and the same way each time.

## How the signals add up

No single signal decides the answer. Assistants look for agreement: the same facts in many places, and outside sources that back up what you say about yourself. That's why the [AI Score](../glossary/index.html#ai-score) looks at all eleven together, and why our [methodology](../methodology/index.html) weighs them as a set. Start with the [complete guide](../guide/index.html) or see the signals that matter most [for your industry](../for/ai/index.html).

From our data · 3D

New data from our research team

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks). [Local AI Registry data](../methodology/index.html)

**1 in 75**

Across the businesses we've scored, nearly two in three land below 45 out of 100 on the AI Score, and barely one in seventy-five clears 65. [What is an AI Score?](../journal/what-is-an-ai-score/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

# How do I know what AI says about my business?

> Ask it, regularly and the same way each time. Run the questions your customers ask across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google's AI answers, Perplexity and others every.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/ai-monitoring/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 11 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Ask it, regularly and the same way each time. Run the questions your customers ask across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google's AI answers, Perplexity and others every month, and record whether you're named, how you're described and which sources each assistant cites.

## Why monitoring matters

AI answers change. Assistants update their models, change their sources and refresh their data. A business that was recommended last month can disappear without warning. Monitoring is how you notice, and the sources each assistant cites tell you exactly where to work next.

New data from our research team

**two-thirds**

Rewording the same local question changed about two-thirds of the sources Google's AI cited. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**29%**

When ChatGPT got the same local question about 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses it named appeared in both answers (8ight.AI, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**0.46**

Asked the same query twice, Google Search shared 0.78 of its sources, AI Overviews 0.66 and Gemini 0.46 (Grossman et al., SIGIR 2026, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions, and [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html), our screenshots of ChatGPT's answers. Every number links to its chart.

[**~35%** of cited sources stayed the same when the same question was worded differently](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording)[**2 of 10** US cities got the same #1 surgeon in six ChatGPT asks of one question](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**87.8%** of local AI claims were supported by the pages the AI cited](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-overview-claim-accuracy-local-vs-other-heatmap)

**Different wording, different sources, same answer.** Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer.Illustration 5, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

**Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated.Figure 20, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

**Local AI answers were more faithful to their sources than average.** 87.8% of 2,253 local claims were supported by the cited pages, versus 84.5% of 95,767 other claims. Faithful to sources is not the same as accurate for your location.Figure 21, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-overview-claim-accuracy-local-vs-other-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-overview-claim-accuracy-local-vs-other-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-overview-claim-accuracy-local-vs-other-heatmap.png)

## What we do for you

Once a month we ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions your customers ask, and we keep the answer each one gave.

A question is a category, not a phrase. You pick the searches you want to win, and we write a set of questions around each one: what it costs, whether it is worth doing, who does it near the town, how to choose a provider.

ChatGPT and Perplexity are asked in a real browser and we keep a screenshot. Gemini is checked directly, so we keep its words but no picture.

We read every answer for your business name and save it under the question that produced it. If a month's check didn't run, it stays blank instead of guessing.

### What you get

- A page of your questions with the current answer under each one.
- The screenshot, for every answer a browser capture landed, so you can see the assistant said it rather than take our word for it.
- Whether you were named, and who was named instead.
- A month by month line for each question, so a change is visible rather than argued.

### How it runs

1. **Your questions are chosen** You pick the searches that matter. We rank your full set by what it is worth commercially, collapse near-identical phrasings, and take the top ten.
2. **Each one is anchored to your town** A question is asked the way a person in your area would ask it, so the answer we record is the answer someone near you would get.
3. **The assistants are asked** ChatGPT and Perplexity in a browser with a screenshot, Gemini checked directly. A question is asked once per calendar month, so nothing is bought twice.
4. **The answer is read and stored** We record the answer text, the businesses named in it, and where you came in. If a check fails, we record it as a failed check, never as you not being named.

**Why it moves the AI answer** Capture is the measurement, not the work. It tells you which questions you already win, and it is the only honest way to know whether the rest of the work moved anything.

## Your monthly report

Every thirty days you get a PDF of what was done on your account and what moved, counted from the day you bought rather than from the first of the month.

One document holding the period: the work ledger, your rankings, the AI answers we captured, your reviews, your directories and the publications that carried you.

Your period is your own. A customer who bought on the 9th is owed one on the 9th, and the pass checks every day rather than firing on the 1st.

A person reads it before you do. Three days before your date the draft goes to your assigned expert and to two people here, and that window is when a wrong sentence gets corrected or the report gets held.

- A PDF on your own date, emailed to everyone you have listed.
- The work ledger for the period, item by item.
- The AI answers captured that month, with the screenshots.
- Rankings, reviews, directories and press, in one place.

## How to do it

1. Write 10 to 20 questions real customers ask, like "best [service] near [neighborhood]" or "who does [service] in [city]".
2. Ask each one in each assistant you care about, from a logged-out browser where possible.
3. Record: named or not, the words used to describe you, and every source cited.
4. Repeat monthly and compare.

# Do best-of lists affect which business AI recommends?

> Often, yes. When someone asks an assistant for "the best" business of a type in a city, it frequently reads local best-of lists and guides to answer.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/best-of-guides/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 10 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Often, yes. When someone asks an assistant for "the best" business of a type in a city, it frequently reads local best-of lists and guides to answer. Businesses that appear on several of those lists are much more likely to be named.

## Why lists carry so much weight

A best-of list is already an answer to the exact question the customer asked. It's easy for an assistant to read three lists, see which businesses appear on most of them and recommend those. If you're on none, you're relying on other signals to overcome that.

# Why do directory listings matter for AI recommendations?

> AI assistants compare what different websites say about your business.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/directory-listings/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 01 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** AI assistants compare what different websites say about your business. When your name, address, phone number and hours match on every directory, the assistant can be confident it has the right business. When they conflict, it hedges or names someone else.

## What AI is checking

Before an assistant recommends a local business, it has to be sure the business is real, open and where it says it is. It checks that by reading many sources at once: maps apps, review sites, industry directories, data aggregators and your own website. Each one is a vote. Matching votes build confidence; mismatched votes create doubt.

The most common mismatches are small: an old suite number, a former phone number, holiday hours that never got changed back, or a business name written three different ways.

New data from our research team

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**83.6%**

83.6% of local AI answers told people to check with their local store, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**3.5%**

Only 3.5% of businesses ChatGPT named in localized searches appeared at every test point across a town (BrightLocal, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**~35%** of cited sources stayed the same when the same question was worded differently](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording)[**83.6%** of local AI answers told people to check with their local store](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle)[**1 of 207** local AI answers gave a street address or phone number](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle)

**One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.Illustration 6, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

**Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated.Figure 20, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

## What we do for you

We check which directories already carry your business, then order listings on the ones that do not.

Twenty three general hosts for everyone: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Your trade adds its own on top, which takes a medical practice to forty: Zocdoc, Healthgrades, WebMD, RealSelf, Vitals and eleven more.

A reading says what we found. A directory we could not find you on is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not present, and we say which one it is.

Readings age out after thirty days, so a page you look at today is a recent read rather than a number from when you signed up.

### What you get

- A page listing each directory and where you stand on it.
- A submission order covering only the ones you are missing.
- One record pushed out, so the phone number is the same everywhere it is printed.
- A re-check whenever you or your expert asks for one, and readings retired at thirty days rather than shown stale.

### How it runs

1. **You confirm the two fields that print** Phone and address. A directory submission prints both and a wrong one is slow and expensive to take back, so nothing is ordered until you have confirmed them.
2. **The presence audit runs** Every host on your roster is checked, so the order covers only what is genuinely missing.
3. **The order is queued** Queued, never auto-confirmed. A person on our team confirms every purchase, under a spending limit, so nothing buys itself.
4. **Progress shows on your page** Premium lists each directory once it is live, under Directory submissions. There is no email for this, because a queue is not news.

**Why it moves the AI answer** An assistant does not read one source. It reads many, and a business whose address disagrees across them is a business it has reason to leave out.

## How to check yours

1. Search your business name plus your city in Google, Bing and Apple Maps.
2. Open the first two pages of results and write down the name, address, phone and hours each one shows.
3. Mark every line that differs from your own website.
4. Ask ChatGPT and Gemini for your phone number and hours. If they get it wrong, a directory is feeding them the wrong data.

# Does my Google Business Profile affect AI recommendations?

> Yes, heavily for Google's own AI answers and Gemini, which draw on Google's local data, and indirectly for other assistants that read Google results.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/google-profile/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

**Short answer** Yes, heavily for Google's own AI answers and Gemini, which draw on Google's local data, and indirectly for other assistants that read Google results. A complete, accurate and active profile is one of the highest-value fixes for any local business.

## Why it matters beyond Google Maps

Your Google Business Profile is the most widely read record of your business on the internet. [Google's AI answers](../../ai/google-ai-overviews/index.html) and [Gemini](../../ai/gemini/index.html) lean on it directly. Other assistants often see it through search results. When it's thin or out of date, every assistant gets a weaker picture of you.

## What we do for you

We write the posts on your Google Business Profile and send each one to you before it publishes.

A post is drafted from things we hold about you: the services on your listing, the searches you picked, your photos and your brand rules. Nothing is written from a template.

Every draft is checked against our writing standard, then by an automatic check that blocks the usual mistakes: the wrong town, a made-up statistic or a medical claim.

You choose the cadence. Daily, a few times a week, weekly, or paused.

### What you get

- A draft in your approvals queue with the question it is aimed at named on it.
- An email with the draft and the date it publishes if you leave it alone.
- Edit, approve or decline. A declined draft is not published and the next one takes a different angle.
- The published post on your listing, with the date and the text kept on your account.

### How it runs

1. **A slot comes due** Your cadence decides when. A post drafted inside the same window is not drafted again, so a weekly cadence is a post a week and not a post a day.
2. **The draft is written and checked** Written from your own facts, then checked and rewritten up to three times until it passes. A draft that still fails on the third pass never reaches your queue, and the next slot tries a different angle.
3. **You see it first** The draft lands in your queue and an email goes to you with a publish date three business days out. If it sits unread, one reminder follows.
4. **It publishes** On approval, or on the date in its email if you leave it alone. Decline it and it doesn't go up. You can set posts to wait for your yes in your settings.

**Why it moves the AI answer** An assistant answering a local question reads the Google listing, and a listing that has said nothing in four months reads as a business that may not be trading.

## Complete every field

- The right primary category, plus every secondary category that fits.
- Every service, each with a short description.
- Hours, including holiday hours.
- Photos of the outside, inside, team and work, labeled clearly.
- Questions and answers filled in by you.

# Can AI understand the photos of my business?

> Partly. AI can now describe images, but it reads the text around a photo more reliably: the file name, alt text, caption and the page it sits on.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/photo-codifying/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 08 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Partly. AI can now describe images, but it reads the text around a photo more reliably: the file name, alt text, caption and the page it sits on. Labeling photos clearly turns them from decoration into evidence of what you do.

## Why labels matter

A photo named IMG\_4821.jpg tells a machine nothing. The same photo named and described as "dental implant consultation room, Irvine" tells it what the room is for and where it is. Multiply that across every photo on your site and profile, and AI gets a much clearer picture of your services and space.

New data from our research team

**78%**

Cited social posts had a median of 8 readable words, and 78% were too thin to verify anything. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**8 words** readable on the median social post Google's AI cited](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source)[**51.6%** of claims citing a store locator or official site had no supporting page](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate)

**What Google’s AI can actually read on a page.** News pages the AI cited had about 500 readable words. Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words.Illustration 4, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

**Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read.** News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin.Figure 18, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

## What we do for you

We collect your photos, write the words that travel with each one, and publish them onto your Google listing a few at a time.

Pictures come from three places: your Google listing, your website, and any social profile we hold a link to. Only public pages, and a private one is stepped past.

Two sets of words are written per photo. One is embedded in the file itself, in the fields Google and every modern library read. The other is the description published under the picture on your listing.

Both use only the words on your own service list and what kind of picture it is. We never let AI write a description of a medical image, and before and after photos are never described at all.

### What you get

- A library with every picture we hold on you, for a person to confirm before anything reaches Google.
- Files carrying your business, your service and your location in their own metadata.
- Photos published onto the listing on a slow cadence, one a day, so a backlog drains over a week rather than in a minute.
- A date per photo you can set yourself.

### How it runs

1. **Photos are collected** From the listing, the website and your social links, once per business. You can upload more at any time.
2. **Each one is classified** Against the services on your own record, so the words we attach are a service you actually offer.
3. **The words are written in** Each file gets a title, description, keywords, your city and a credit. We don't describe what's in the picture.
4. **They publish on a drip** One a day per business. Google limits how fast new photos can go up, and a pile posted in one day looks like spam.

**Why it moves the AI answer** A photo with no words attached is invisible to anything reading rather than looking, and the description under it is the part a retrieval system can quote.

## How to codify a photo

1. Rename the file with plain words for what it shows.
2. Write alt text in one sentence: what is in the picture and why it matters.
3. Add a caption on the page where it helps the reader.
4. Place the photo on the page about that service, not in a generic gallery.

# Does press coverage help a local business get recommended by AI?

> Yes. AI assistants trust independent sources more than a business's own website.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/pr/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 02 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Yes. AI assistants trust independent sources more than a business's own website. A real news story or feature that names your business is one of the strongest signals that you are established and worth recommending.

## Why AI weighs the press

Your website will always say you are great. An assistant knows that, so it looks for someone else saying it. Local news, trade publications and respected industry sites act as outside proof. When an assistant searches the web to answer a question, those pages are often among the sources it reads.
