## What we do for you

You choose what the news is, we draft the release, and nothing goes to the wire until you have signed it off.

The topic is yours. A release is irreversible once a wire has it, so we never pick the subject and we never send one without your approval.

The draft is held to the strictest reading of our writing standard. No outcome claim, no credential we do not hold on file, no statistic nobody measured.

Each publication that picks it up is recorded against your account with its address, so the coverage is a list of links rather than a number.

### What you get

- A drafted release on a topic you picked, in your voice.
- A named reminder while it waits, because nothing sends this one for you.
- The publications that carried it, each with the article address.
- The same list printed in your monthly report.

### How it runs

1. **You pick the topic** From your own news. An opening, a new service, a hire, a piece of equipment.
2. **We draft it** The news is the first sentence. The draft carries only facts we hold on you or facts you supplied for this release.
3. **You sign it off** A press release never goes out unless you approve it. If the deadline passes without you sending it, we cancel the order, tell you we did not buy it, and draft a fresh one on the next round.
4. **Coverage is recorded** Every pickup is stored with its publication and its address. If a distributor quotes a reach number, we show it as their number, never as something we measured.

**Why it moves the AI answer** A mention on a publication you do not own is the one kind of evidence about you that you did not write, which is why an assistant weighs it differently from your own site.

## What counts

- Local news stories, features and expert quotes.
- Trade and industry publications.
- Interviews and podcasts with show notes that name you.
- Award lists from real organizations.

Paid press releases that only appear on syndication networks count for much less. They are easy to buy, so they prove little.

# How do reviews affect whether AI recommends my business?

> Reviews are one of the main things assistants use to decide who to recommend.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/reputation/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 06 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Reviews are one of the main things assistants use to decide who to recommend. They look at your rating, how many reviews you have, how recent they are, what customers say in their own words, and whether you reply. Reviews on several sites count more than reviews on one.

## What AI reads in your reviews

An assistant doesn't just see a star rating. It reads review text to learn what you're known for. If customers often mention a service, a staff member or a quality like "on time" or "explained everything", the assistant can repeat that when someone asks for exactly that.

What the screenshots show

- RealSelf appeared among the sources of 27 of 30 full “best rhinoplasty surgeon in [city]” answers we screenshotted across 10 cities on Nov 13, 2026.
- In our Los Angeles runs, a RealSelf rating and review count sat right next to most names ChatGPT recommended.

[See every screenshot in AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html)

New data from our research team

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions, and [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html), our screenshots of ChatGPT's answers. Every number links to its chart.

[**27 of 30** ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**8 words** readable on the median social post Google's AI cited](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source)[**2 of 10** US cities got the same #1 surgeon in six ChatGPT asks of one question](../../answer-watch/index.html)

**Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read.** News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin.Figure 18, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

**Social posts the AI cited had a median of 8 readable words.** The median cited social post had 8 readable words. Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18.Figure 19, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.png)

## What we do for you

We draft a reply to each new three, four and five star review on your Google listing, and you edit, approve or decline it. A reply to a one or two star review is read by our team first, and nothing goes up under your name unless you approve it.

A reply answers the person, not the room. The first sentence responds to what this reviewer said and names what the visit was for. It adds one thing a stranger reading before booking would want, and stops.

A one or two star review is never answered without your approval, at any age. It is flagged to you on your reviews page with what it says, whether it breaks a Google policy and where the removal petition stands. One that lands while you are with us also emails you within hours; one already sitting on the listing when you arrived is flagged without the mail, because a notice about a review from 2019 reads as news and is not.

Thin replies already on your listing are rewritten, up to twenty of them, and never the one under a one or two star review. Four words of thanks under a review that named a treatment is a wasted paragraph on a page an assistant reads.

### What you get

- A drafted reply per unanswered three, four or five star review, newest first.
- A flag on your reviews page for each low-star review, and an email within hours for one less than a fortnight old, with the petition state stated plainly and never overstated.
- The three steps to report a review from your own Google account, because some of them are yours to file and not ours.
- Replies published on your listing under your name.

### How it runs

1. **Reviews are read** The review pass runs every three hours against your Google listing.
2. **Three stars and up are drafted** At most twenty drafts in a run, and at most five a day for reviews older than six months, so a back catalogue is worked through rather than dumped.
3. **One and two stars are pursued** Each one from the last six months is read against Google policy and gets a petition written and assigned to one of our people, because Google only accepts these from a person, so one of our team submits it by hand.
4. **You approve or leave it** Replies to three, four and five star reviews are in the default set that publishes after three business days if untouched. Switch the type to manual and nothing moves without you.

**Why it moves the AI answer** Reviews are the text an assistant quotes when it explains why it picked somebody, and a reply is the only part of that text you get to write.

## What helps most

- A steady flow of new reviews, not a burst once a year.
- Reviews on more than one site: Google plus the review sites your industry uses.
- Customers naming the service they came for.
- A short, personal reply to every review, good or bad.

# Is SEO still needed if customers use AI instead of Google?

> Yes. Many assistants search the web before they answer, and they lean on the pages that already rank well.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/seo/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 04 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Yes. Many assistants search the web before they answer, and they lean on the pages that already rank well. Google's own AI answers are built on Google search results. Strong SEO is often how a page becomes a source for AI in the first place.

## How SEO and AI connect

When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity a local question, the assistant often runs a web search behind the scenes, reads the top results and writes an answer from them. If your pages don't show up in those searches, the assistant may never read them. That is why [AI visibility and SEO](../../signals/seo/index.html) overlap so much: SEO gets you into the reading list, AI visibility gets you into the answer.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**147 vs 70** times a store's own site ranked on page one, vs times the AI cited it, across 157 brand questions](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews)[**4.1%** of business-site citations came from beyond Google's first page](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source)[**6.5%** of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap)

**SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.** Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links.Illustration 1, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

**Ranked first, still skipped: why SEO alone isn’t AEO.** In 147 of 157 brand questions the store’s own site ranked on page one, but the AI cited it in only 70. Ranking and being used by AI are separate outcomes.Illustration 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.png)

**Ranked and used vs ranked and ignored: a 2x2 of brand websites.** Most brands ranked on page one nearly every time. What split them was use: Publix, Trader Joe’s and Sam’s Club were cited every time; Walmart, Starbucks and Chipotle were ranked but ignored.Figure 11, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2.png)

## What we do for you

We work on the search rankings that sit under every AI answer: your service pages, the links pointing at them and the technical fixes that let assistants find and cite you.

- A page for each service you want to win, written from your own facts
- Technical fixes that stop crawlers and assistants from missing pages
- Every change dated in your monthly report

## What matters most for a local business

- One page per main service, written in the words customers use.
- A page for each location, with its address, hours and map.
- Answers to real questions near the top of each page.
- Fast pages that work well on a phone.
- Links from other local and industry sites.

## Where SEO stops

Ranking is not the same as being recommended. An assistant can read your top-ranking page and still name a competitor with better [reviews](../../signals/reputation/index.html) or more [outside mentions](../../signals/third-party-articles/index.html). SEO is one signal of eleven.

# Why do articles on other websites matter for AI visibility?

> Assistants trust what independent sites say about you more than what you say about yourself.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/third-party-articles/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 09 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Assistants trust what independent sites say about you more than what you say about yourself. Articles, interviews, guides and partner pages that name your business give AI outside confirmation of who you are and what you're good at.

## Outside proof

When an assistant builds an answer, it pulls from several sources and favors ones that agree. If a local magazine, a partner's blog and an industry guide all describe you the same way, that description becomes the one AI repeats.

New data from our research team

**0.737**

In a 75,000-brand study, the top correlate of AI visibility was YouTube and branded web mentions (0.737), not links or pages (Ahrefs, cited in our white paper The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**67.5%**

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**67.5%** of citations in local AI answers came from news coverage](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration)[**4.1%** of business-site citations came from beyond Google's first page](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source)[**7.2** sources cited per local AI answer, versus 8.1 for other topics](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#sources-per-ai-overview-answer-distribution)

**How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business.** For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store.Illustration 2, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

**Local gatekeepers: which sources dominate Google AI’s local answers.** Gannett newspapers and other news outlets are local gatekeepers: large shares of local citations and over-represented versus other topics. Business sites sit near the bottom left.Figure 8, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answer-source-2x2-share-vs-lift), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answer-source-2x2-share-vs-lift.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answer-source-2x2-share-vs-lift.png)

**The AI goes past page one for news, not for business websites.** Only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside Google’s first page, versus 48.8% for AOL/Yahoo/MSN and 39.8% for TEGNA stations. A business site has to rank to be used.Figure 13, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source.png)

## What we do for you

We get your business written about on sites you don't own, because a mention elsewhere is evidence an assistant weighs differently from your own website.

- Articles on relevant outside sites, about real things you do
- Only facts you have confirmed, never an outcome claim
- Every placement listed with its link in your monthly report

## Where these come from

- Local magazines, blogs and community sites.
- Suppliers and partners who feature their customers.
- Industry associations and member directories.
- Guest articles written by you on respected sites.
- Local event and sponsorship pages.

Ask that each article uses your exact business name, city and a link to the page about the service it mentions. Consistency here reinforces your [listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html) and makes it easy for AI to connect the article to your [entity](../../glossary/index.html#entity).

# Does video help my business show up in AI answers?

> Video helps in two ways. Assistants that search the web can read video titles, descriptions and transcripts, and YouTube results often appear in Google's A.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/video/

**Short answer** Video helps in two ways. Assistants that search the web can read video titles, descriptions and transcripts, and YouTube results often appear in Google's AI answers. A clear video that answers a real customer question gives AI one more trustworthy source about you.

## What AI reads from a video

Most assistants don't watch your video. They read its title, description, captions and the page it sits on. A video titled "Lobby tour" says nothing. A video titled with the exact question a customer asks, with accurate captions, answers it.

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin.Figure 18, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words.Illustration 4, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

# What does my website need so AI can understand it?

> Your site needs to load fast, work on a phone, state plainly what you do and where, and include structured data (schema) that labels your business, service.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/web-management/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 05 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Your site needs to load fast, work on a phone, state plainly what you do and where, and include structured data (schema) that labels your business, services, hours and reviews in a format machines read without guessing.

## What AI needs from your site

Assistants and search crawlers read your site's code, not its design. They need clear facts: who you are, what services you offer, where, when you're open and how to book. Structured data, often called [schema markup](../../glossary/index.html#schema-markup), states those facts in a standard format so there's nothing to guess.

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What we do for you

We keep your website accurate and readable for AI: service pages, schema markup, speed and mobile fixes. If a web team or studio already runs your site, we work alongside them instead of replacing them.

- Service and FAQ schema on the pages that matter
- Hours, prices and team kept in step with your verified record
- Speed and mobile fixes, listed in your monthly report

- Pages load quickly on a phone.

# AI visibility for cannabis dispensaries

> When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near them, we work to have you in the answer. Free AI Score, then the work that moves it.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/for/cannabis-dispensaries/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Dispensaries

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Dispensaries are locked out of most paid channels, which makes being named in an answer worth more here than in any other trade on this list.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near you, you're in the answer.

## What dispensaries are up against

Google Ads will not take you. Meta will not take you. What is left is the organic answer, and the organic answer is increasingly one an assistant writes.

People ask by landmark and by neighborhood far more than they ask by city. Almost every high-volume question we hold in this trade names a park, a station or a mall.

People also do not say "cannabis dispensary". They say dispo, or here, or nothing at all, and the questions we ask on your behalf are asked in those words.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

A new three star and up review gets a reply drafted in your voice for approval. A low-star review is flagged with a policy read on it, and any reply to one waits for your approval.

Your questions asked monthly with the screenshots kept, which is the only evidence available in a channel with no ad platform to report on.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. We are a multi-doctor practice. Does each doctor get a page?

The registry entry is the practice. Credentials for individual doctors are facts you supply, and they go on your listing rather than being written by us.

Can you say we are board certified?

Only if you have given us the certification. A credential we do not hold on file is the one thing we will never approximate.

Eye care

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for an eye doctor near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Eye care is the largest trade in the registry, and the question people ask an assistant is almost never the name of a practice. It is who is near me, who takes my insurance, and what an exam costs.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for an eye doctor near you, you're in the answer.

## What eye care practices are up against

Optometrists, ophthalmologists and lasik surgeons are one market to the person asking. An assistant answering "eye doctor near me" does not sort by degree, so a practice competing only against its own profession is competing against a third of the field.

Insurance is the second question, every time. A listing that does not say which plans it takes loses the answer to one that does.

## Why AI matters for med spas

Med spa clients research hard before they book, because treatments touch their face and their budget. Many now ask an assistant to shortlist providers, compare prices and check safety. The assistant names a few businesses, and most clients never look past them.

## Rules med spas need to follow

Name your medical director and licensed injectors with their credentials; trust signals matter more in medical aesthetics than almost anywhere. Follow your state's rules on who can perform each treatment, and get written consent before posting any before and after photo. Use brand names like Botox correctly and avoid promising results.

## Frequently asked questions

Should I list prices on my website?

Where you can, yes. Price is one of the most common questions clients ask AI. A clear starting price or range helps assistants answer with your business in mind.

Do before and after photos help with AI?

They help clients more than machines. Label them clearly, follow consent rules and place them on the page for that treatment.

How long does it take for a med spa to show up in AI?

It depends on where you start and how competitive your area is. Fixes to your facts and profile can show up within weeks; reviews, lists and articles build over months. Our [90-day guarantee](../../../guarantee/index.html) reflects that timeline.

# AI visibility for medical clinics

> When someone asks ChatGPT for a clinic near them, we work to have you in the answer. Free AI Score, then the work that moves it.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/for/medical-clinics/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Medical clinics

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for a medical clinic near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Most people asking an assistant for a clinic are asking about today: who is open, who is near, who takes their insurance. Hours and address decide more of these answers than anything you write.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a medical clinic near you, you're in the answer.

## What medical clinics are up against

The heaviest demand a clinic sits under is urgent, and it is asked in urgent-care words rather than clinic words. A clinic that does walk-ins and does not say so loses those answers to a business that does.

Hours that disagree between your listing and your site are the single most common gap we find, and it is the cheapest one to close.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What people ask AI about medical clinics

These are the questions people put to ChatGPT, Gemini and Google about medical clinics, ranked by how often they're searched. None of them names a business. The assistant decides who to name.

| The question | Searches a year |
| --- | --- |
| Is there an urgent care facility nearby? | 180,000 |
| Where can I find a medical clinic near me? | 29,520 |
| Which medical clinic is closest to me? | 29,520 |

## What we do for medical clinics

The work that matters most here, and the feature page that explains each one in full.

### [Directory listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

One record pushed everywhere, so the phone number and the address read the same on every directory an answer might be assembled from.

### [Posts](../../signals/google-profile/index.html)

Posts that state the services, the hours and whether you take walk-ins, on the page an assistant reads first.

### [Review replies](../../signals/reputation/index.html)

A new three star and up review gets a reply drafted for your approval. A one or two star review is flagged to you with a policy read on it, and any reply to one waits for your approval.

From our data · 3D

## What people ask AI about medical clinics

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for medical clinics

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Because AI reads you as a medical practice, your roster grows to 40, adding Zocdoc, Healthgrades, WebMD, RealSelf, Vitals and more. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

1. **Week 1: the baseline** We ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions above, anchored to your town, and keep the screenshots. You see who is named today, and whether you are.
2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.
3. **Every week: the work** Posts, review replies and photos go to your approval queue. Nothing goes live without your OK.
4. **Day 90: the check** If AI isn't naming you, we keep working free until it does.

## Frequently asked questions

We are a clinic, not urgent care. Does that matter?

It matters for what we write. The demand is worded as urgent care and your listing should say plainly what you do and do not do, rather than borrowing a word that would misdescribe you.

How quickly do hours changes reach the assistants?

Your listing updates immediately. What an assistant says catches up on its own schedule, which is why we re-ask your questions every month and show you the answer.

## Questions surgeons ask us

How does ChatGPT decide which plastic surgeons to recommend?

It recommends surgeons it can verify. That means the same facts on Google, directories and review sites, a board certification it can confirm, procedures it can match to the question, and recent reviews. When those sources disagree or say little, it leaves you out.

Is this different from regular SEO?

Yes. SEO gets your website ranked in a list of links. AI search reads many sources at once and names only a few surgeons. You need both. We focus on the part most agencies miss: what AI reads about you away from your own website.

Will this work with my current marketing agency?

Yes. We do not replace your website, ads or social media. We handle the listings, reviews, credentials and monthly AI checks that agencies usually leave alone, and we are happy to share our reports with your agency.

How do you keep review replies HIPAA-safe?

Our replies never confirm that someone is a patient and never mention a procedure or any health details. Every reply lands in your inbox before it goes out, and you have three business days to change it or stop it.

Which AI tools do you track?

ChatGPT, Google Gemini and AI Overviews, Claude and Perplexity. Your monthly report shows what each one says about your practice and what changed.

How long until AI starts naming my practice?

Our goal is about 3 months, and some practices see changes sooner. If AI is not naming you in 90 days, we keep working for free until it does.

## Frequently asked questions

Does a surgeon's personal profile matter?

Yes. Patients often ask about the surgeon by name. A strong individual profile, linked to the practice, helps AI connect the two.

Can I reply to reviews without breaking privacy rules?

Yes, with general replies that don't confirm treatment or share details. When in doubt, take it offline.

How long does it take for a plastic surgery practice to show up in AI?

It depends on where you start and how competitive your area is. Fixes to your facts and profile can show up within weeks; reviews, lists and articles build over months. Our [90-day guarantee](../../../guarantee/index.html) reflects that timeline.

# AI visibility for skin care clinics

Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Skin care clinics

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for a skin care clinic near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Almost every question in this trade is about a condition rather than a clinic, and the businesses named in those answers are the ones whose pages describe the condition.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a skin care clinic near you, you're in the answer.

## What skin care clinics are up against

Dry skin, skin tags, anti-wrinkle treatment and red light therapy are the four topics the demand table holds most of. None of them is a business name.

That is an opportunity and a trap. A page that explains a procedure gets retrieved. A page that promises the procedure will work is an advertising problem.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for skin care clinics

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Because AI reads you as a beauty business, your roster grows to 29 with the beauty and wellness sites your customers use. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.

## Frequently asked questions

Our treatments are on our website already. Why is that not enough?

Retrieval happens at passage level. A services page that lists names without describing them has nothing an answer can quote, which is a different problem from not existing.

Can you write about products we sell?

We can name a product you stock. We cannot say what it will do to somebody, which is where most product copy in this trade goes wrong.

Urgent care

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for urgent care near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Urgent care is the one trade here where the person asking needs an answer in the next hour, and the questions show it. Hours, insurance, wait time, walk-ins.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for urgent care near you, you're in the answer.

## What urgent care centers are up against

The two biggest questions we hold in this trade are hours and insurance, in that order. Neither is about how good you are.

The rest are operational: parking, wait times, whether you handle a fracture, whether you see children, what to bring. An assistant can only answer those off a record that says so.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). ## What we noticed

- **No two answers matched.** Eight different surgeons appeared across three runs of the same question. Only two were named every time.
- **Position moves.** The same surgeon was #1 in one run and #3 in the next. A single screenshot is a snapshot, not a ranking.
- **RealSelf shows up everywhere.** Most entries quoted a RealSelf rating and review count, often as the only source shown.
- **ChatGPT interviews the patient.** After the list, it asked about the result they want, first surgery or revision, and in one run their budget.

That's why we measure how often AI names a business across repeated asks, not where it lands once. It's the same way every client's AI Score is measured.

- **Photos came from anywhere.** Pictures beside named businesses came from directories, a used-truck listing and other companies' websites.
- **The rating in the answer wasn't always the rating on the map.** For three car dealers, ChatGPT quoted a higher Birdeye or DealerRater rating than the Google rating on its own map.
- **Few links.** Facts came from map listings. The pages it linked were mostly licensing boards and best-of lists.

# What Is an AI Score, and How Is It Calculated?

> The AI Score is a 0 to 100 measure of how findable and recommendable a local business is to AI assistants, built from eight published signals.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/journal/what-is-an-ai-score/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Journal

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

---

## What the AI Score measures

The AI Score is a single number, from 0 to 100, that measures how findable and recommendable a local business is to AI assistants like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews. It is the metric we built Local AI Registry around, and we publish exactly how it is calculated. A high score means AI can find you, trust you, and name you when a customer asks; a low score means it cannot.

The number matters because the results are stark. Across the local businesses we have scored, nearly two in three land below 45 out of 100, and barely one in seventy-five clears 65. Most local businesses are not close to being recommendable by AI, and most owners have no idea where they stand.

64%of the local businesses we scored land below 45 out of 100

The AI Score exists to turn that invisible problem into one number you can see, act on, and track. It is the answer to the question every owner now has to ask: [does AI recommend me, and why not?](https://localairegistry.com/journal/how-ai-decides-which-local-business-to-recommend)

## The eight signals behind the score

The AI Score is not a black box or a single-metric gimmick. It is built from eight signals, each measuring a different part of whether an assistant can find and recommend you. Every weight is documented in our [scoring methodology](../../methodology/index.html).

- Retrieval grounding: can AI find and cite you for the queries that drive bookings, not just your brand name.
- Off-property attestation: what independent sources across the web say about you.
- AI visibility: whether specific assistants already name you today.
- Reviews: volume, recency, rating, and whether you respond to them.
- Google Business Profile: how complete and accurate your listing is.
- Authority: the quality of the sites that link to and reference you.
- Speed and mobile: whether your site is technically eligible to be cited.
- Content and schema: whether your pages are clear and machine-readable.

The first two signals, retrieval grounding and off-property attestation, carry the most weight, because they are what actually decide an AI recommendation. The other six are eligibility: necessary, but not sufficient.

## How the number is calculated

Each signal is scored on its own, then combined into the final 0-to-100 number using a weighted geometric mean rather than a simple average. The distinction matters. A geometric mean leans on your weakest signal, so a business cannot paper over a missing off-property presence with a fast website. If any load-bearing signal is near zero, the overall score stays low, which mirrors how an assistant actually behaves: one strong attribute does not earn a recommendation when a critical one is absent.

The weights come from how much each signal moves a real AI recommendation, not from what is easiest to measure. That is why two businesses with identical websites can score very differently: the one the wider web corroborates scores higher, because corroboration is what the assistant grounds its answer in.

## What a good AI Score looks like

Because most local businesses score low, the bar to stand out is lower than it looks. Roughly:

- A score of 65 or above is good: AI can reliably find and recommend you. Very few businesses are here yet.
- A score in the 45 to 64 range is fair: you are eligible and sometimes named, with clear gaps to close.
- Below 45 is poor: AI struggles to find or trust you, and a competitor is getting the recommendation instead.

The point of the number is not the grade, it is the diagnosis. Your AI Score comes with the specific signals dragging it down, so you know what to fix first.

## Why the score is independent

No business can buy a higher AI Score, and no one can pay to be removed from a competitor’s comparison. We [never sell rank](../../trust/index.html), and we publish the method so anyone can check our work. That independence is the whole point: a score you could buy would tell an assistant nothing, and it would tell you nothing either.

## Common questions

### What is a good AI Score?

Broadly, 65 or above is good, 45 to 64 is fair, and below 45 is poor. Because most local businesses currently score below 45, even reaching the fair range puts you ahead of the majority of your competitors.

### Is checking my AI Score free?

Yes. You can look up any business and see its AI Score for nothing.

### How is an AI Score different from a Google ranking?

A Google ranking is your position in a list of blue links. An AI Score measures whether an assistant will name you at all when it answers a question with a single recommendation instead of a list. The signals overlap, but the outcome an AI Score predicts is being the answer, not being on page one.

### Can I improve my AI Score?

Yes, and the score tells you how. It surfaces which of the eight signals are weakest, so you fix the ones that move an AI recommendation first, chiefly retrieval grounding and off-property attestation.

### How often is the AI Score updated?

It reflects the most recent measurement of what assistants say and the underlying signals. As you improve a signal, or as the assistants change, the score is recalculated so it stays a current read rather than a one-time snapshot.

# Methodology: How the AI Score Is Built

> Eight signals, one number from 0 to 100. The heaviest is whether AI can retrieve you at all. Every input, weight, formula, and source, documented.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/methodology/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Methodology

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

The thesis

## One number. One mechanism.

AI assistants don’t recommend the closest business, the prettiest website, or whoever paid the most. They recommend a business they can retrieve and recognize as real: one that many independent, trustworthy sources describe the same way.

Because retrieval is the gate everything else passes through, the single heaviest signal is whether you appear in the results an AI model pulls from when it answers. Everything else either earns that retrievability or refines what the AI says once you’re in.

Retrievability isn’t one ranking factor among many. It’s the precondition for all of them.

The weights

## How much each signal weighs.

Eight signals, identical for every business, ordered by how much each one moves an AI recommendation. The single heaviest is whether you can be retrieved at all.

Retrievability and the attestation that earns it are the retrieval tier, together 46% of the score. Nearly half.

It measures how likely AI engines are to recommend a business, and how accurately. The same method scores every business on the registry. Every business is scored the same way, and nobody can pay for a better score. Fair starts at 45, good at 65.

Retrieval tier
26%Retrieval groundingWhether you appear in the ranked results AI retrieves and cites: AI-Overview citations, organic top-10 for your money queries, and the Bing index ChatGPT leans on.
20%Off-property attestationVolume and consistency of what others say about you: YouTube mentions, branded web mentions, third-party “best-of” lists. The cause of retrievability.
14%AI visibilityWhether ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and AI Overviews name you, and whether they name you for the right service.
12%Reviews & responseThe star average is only one input. We also read volume, velocity, the specificity of review language, and response cadence. Specific reviews are what AI quotes verbatim.
8%Backlink & citation authorityDomain authority and editorial quality of the sources that attest to you.
8%Google Business ProfileRequired and recommended fields; update cadence. The listing AI pulls from first.
7%Speed & mobileCore Web Vitals at the 75th percentile, on a real phone.
5%Content freshness & schemaCrawl recency, intent alignment, valid JSON-LD, canonicals.

Methods referenced

## We didn’t invent the math.

Every part of the score is a named, published method, borrowed from information retrieval, index construction, and game theory, and each one is cited.

Fig. 8, Methods composing the AI Score · n = 10 · 3 stages · [full citations](../methodology/index.html#references)

Reading a business page

## What the marks on a business page mean

Every fact on a business page carries one of three marks, and every mark points to a reference at the end of that page.

Confirmedsolid circle
:   From a known source: the business's website, its Google Business Profile, review sites like Yelp, Healthgrades and RealSelf, a licensing board, or measured by Local AI Registry.

Visitor submittedhollow circle
:   Added or corrected by a person, with the date and how they know, like a phone call or a visit.

AI guesshollow triangle
:   What AI engines like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity are saying right now. Nobody has confirmed it.

Each row is marked Confirmed, Visitor submitted or AI guess, with where it came from. Each reference names the fact, the source, what kind of source it is, and the date it was checked, with a link and an archived copy so anyone can verify it. Visitor references are dated firsthand accounts. AI guesses record what an AI engine said on that date, not what is true.

How AI reads a business

## How AI decides what to tell you about a med spa

When you ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Google for a med spa, the AI doesn't visit each business. It reads what's already written about it: the business's website, its Google Business Profile, review sites like Yelp and RealSelf, news stories, licensing boards and directories like ours. Then it repeats what those sources agree on.

That's why AI gets small facts wrong. If Yelp says a place is open Mondays and the website says it isn't, the AI has to pick one. Each business page on the registry lists the answers that disagree with what we've confirmed.

The more sources agree, and the more specific they are, the more confidently AI recommends a business. A review that says "the nurse did half a syringe in my lips and it looks natural" is far more useful to an AI than one that says "great place."

## How AI decides what to tell you about an eye surgery practice

When you ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Google for an eye surgeon, the AI doesn't visit the practice. It reads what's already written about it: the practice's website, its Google Business Profile, review sites like Healthgrades and Yelp, your state's medical and optometry boards, news stories and directories like ours. Then it repeats what those sources agree on.

That's why AI gets small facts wrong. If one site says a surgeon still operates there and the practice's own website doesn't list them, the AI has to pick one. Each business page on the registry lists the answers that disagree with what we've confirmed.

The more sources agree, and the more specific they are, the more confidently AI recommends a practice. A review that says "my surgeon did my cataract surgery on a Tuesday and I was driving by Friday" is far more useful to an AI than one that says "great doctor."

# The $199 Botox studio on Newport Boulevard

> QUIKTOX, a surgeon-led Costa Mesa studio, charges one flat $199 price for Botox in a city that charges by the unit.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/news/the-199-botox-studio-on-newport-boulevard/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

## Overview

**QUIKTOX** (also QUIKTOX Injection Studio) is a medical spa in Costa Mesa, California, that specializes in flat-price Botox. It opened in 2024 in a Sola Salon Studios suite on Newport Boulevard and is directed by Johnathan Slone, MD, a board-certified surgeon. Founded and funded by neurotoxin industry veterans, it lists Botox at $199 a treatment or $45 a month.

Local AI Registry verdict · [Best value, Best Botox in Costa Mesa 2026](../../best/botox/costa-mesa-ca/)

The clearest-priced Botox in Costa Mesa

QUIKTOX is the best pick in Costa Mesa for Botox at a set price you know before you sit down: one flat $199 treatment or a $45 monthly membership, with a board-certified surgeon as medical director. It suits first-timers and budget-minded patients. It's a small single-suite studio with few public reviews so far, so people who want lasers, facials or a large menu should look at a full-service med spa.

## QUIKTOX for your situation

Direct answers for the specific things people ask.

### First-time Botox

QUIKTOX suits first-timers because the price is set before the visit: $199 flat, with the process explained first, according to its Giftly business summary.

### Botox on a budget in Costa Mesa

QUIKTOX's flat $199 is below the $200 to $400 the 20-unit frown-line dose costs at typical per-unit rates, and the $45 monthly membership lowers it further for regulars.

### Lunch-break Botox near Newport Boulevard

QUIKTOX is on Newport Boulevard between 17th and 18th Street, and reviewers describe visits as quick enough to fit into a workday.

### Saturday Botox in Costa Mesa

QUIKTOX lists Saturday hours, 9 am to 5 pm, on Yelp and its own Botox page.

### Botox before a wedding or event

Botox reaches full effect in about two weeks, so book QUIKTOX at least 14 days before the date.

### Botox near Hoag Hospital or John Wayne Airport

QUIKTOX is about 1.2 miles from Hoag Hospital Newport Beach and 3.9 miles from John Wayne Airport, in a straight line.

### Ongoing Botox every three to four months

QUIKTOX's $45 monthly membership is the cheapest in Costa Mesa and is built for regulars; most Botox lasts three to four months.

### Surgeon-supervised Botox at a low price

QUIKTOX's medical director, Johnathan Slone, MD, is a board-certified surgeon with California license A98613, which is unusual at a $199 price point.

## What Botox costs here, by area

FDA-labeled doses for each area, what that dose costs at per-unit prices, and how QUIKTOX's flat price compares.

| Area | FDA-labeled dose | At $10 to $20 a unit | At QUIKTOX |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frown lines (glabellar) | 20 units | $200 to $400 | $199 flat |
| Crow's feet (lateral canthal) | 24 units | $240 to $480 | $199 flat |
| Forehead lines, with frown lines | 40 units total | $400 to $800 | Ask |
| Neck bands (platysma) | 26 to 36 units | $260 to $720 | Ask |

### What to expect

Botox Cosmetic usually starts working within a few days, reaches full effect in about two weeks and lasts around three to four months. Doses above follow the FDA prescribing information; the injector sets the actual dose at the visit.

QUIKTOX on Newport Boulevard charges a flat $199 per treatment, the lowest published price for a standard Botox treatment in Costa Mesa, and offers the city's cheapest membership at $45 a month.

Johnathan Slone, MD, a board-certified surgeon with California medical license A98613 and NPI 1548419484.

### What are QUIKTOX's hours?

Most sources list Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 5 pm, closed Sunday. Some listings show fewer days, so call (949) 229-2275 to confirm.

### Does QUIKTOX offer a Botox membership?

Yes. QUIKTOX lists a Botox membership at $45 a month, the lowest-priced in Costa Mesa.

### Is QUIKTOX a medical spa or a salon?

QUIKTOX is a physician-directed medical spa. It operates from a suite inside a Sola Salon Studios building, so some directories list it under salons.

### Does QUIKTOX offer peptide consultations?

Yes. Since October 2026 QUIKTOX offers free peptide consultations through partner providers.

### How far is QUIKTOX from John Wayne Airport?

About 3.9 miles in a straight line from John Wayne Airport (SNA), and about 1.2 miles from Hoag Hospital Newport Beach.

### What other med spas offer Botox in Costa Mesa?

Medical spas ranking for Botox in Costa Mesa include Skin Perfect Medical, Glo Bar Med Spa, TIEV, Bellevie Medical, Newport Med Center and Iconique Med Spa.

### How do I book at QUIKTOX?

QUIKTOX books appointments online through Vagaro, or by phone at (949) 229-2275.

### How long does Botox from QUIKTOX last?

Botox Cosmetic usually lasts about three to four months, reaching full effect around two weeks after treatment.

### Can I use HSA or FSA money for Botox at QUIKTOX?

No. Cosmetic Botox is not an eligible medical expense under IRS rules.

### How many units of Botox do frown lines need?

The FDA-labeled dose for frown lines is 20 units. At $10 to $20 a unit that's $200 to $400; QUIKTOX lists a flat $199.

# The Convergence

> White Paper 03 from Local AI Registry Research reads eleven independent streams of evidence on how local businesses get recommended by AI, explained twice.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/proof/the-convergence-white-paper/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

White paper 03

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

---

## How to read this report

### The view from above, and how it's written

Most research on AI search reports one study at a time. This report does the opposite. It gathers every bucket of evidence we could find on how local businesses get recommended by AI, lays them on one table, and steps back until the whole picture resolves. From that altitude, the disconnected facts collapse into a single conclusion and four currents that run beneath all of them.

Because the goal is to be useful to a business owner and defensible to a skeptic, every section is written twice. In Plain Terms states the point in language anyone can act on. The Proof then establishes it rigorously, naming the specific researcher, study, court record, or dataset behind each claim, with the chart that shows it.

### How every claim is labelled

- **CITED** A figure from a named, linkable source. Real or omitted, never invented.
- **ANALYSIS** Our own conclusion from reading the sources together.
- **PROJECTION** A forward inference from a measured trend. Flagged, never disguised as data.

## I · The Convergence, eleven streams, one substrate

### In Plain Terms

We pulled together every kind of evidence we could find about how AI decides which local businesses to recommend, what shoppers do, what the data shows, what Google's own people and documents say, what scientists have proven about how these systems retrieve information, and what the law now requires. They come from totally different places and were never meant to be read together. But when you put them side by side, they all say the same thing: AI doesn't recommend a website, a profile, or whoever is closest. It recommends a business it can recognize as real, one that many trustworthy sources independently describe the same way. Being that recognizable, verifiable business is the whole game.

### The Proof

The diagram below places eleven independent research streams around a single center. Each was produced by different people, with different methods, for different reasons. Read individually they are a pile of disconnected facts. Read together they converge, every one of them describes, from its own angle, the same underlying object: the verifiable entity.

**Figure I · The convergence.** Eleven independent streams; each source named below and in References.

Here is who and what each stream is, and what it independently establishes **CITED**, the named evidence behind the picture:

**BrightLocal.** Local Consumer Review Survey 2026. 45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery (up from 6%), and 88% fact-check the result, so people seek, then verify, a recommendation.¹

45%of consumers now use AI for local discovery (up from 6%). CITED: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey 2026.
88%fact-check the result. CITED: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey 2026.

**Glenn Allsopp · Ahrefs.** 75,000-brand visibility study. The top correlate of AI visibility is YouTube and branded web mentions (0.737), not links or pages, the signal is off-site, distributed conversation.²

0.737The top correlate of AI visibility is YouTube and branded web mentions. CITED: Glenn Allsopp, Ahrefs, 75,000-brand visibility study.

**Ahrefs · 146M SERPs.** AI Overview trigger study. Specific, conversational, entity-rich questions trigger AI answers far more than bare keywords (57.9% vs 9.5%).³

57.9%full question-style queries trigger an AI Overview. CITED: Ahrefs, What Triggers AI Overviews? 86 Factors, 146M SERPs.
9.5%single-word searches trigger an AI Overview. CITED: Ahrefs, What Triggers AI Overviews? 86 Factors, 146M SERPs.

**Local Falcon.** ~60,000 simulations. Distance from the searcher correlates with AI rank at r = 0.001, proximity, the old master variable, is gone; what remains is authority.⁵

r = 0.001Distance from the searcher correlates with AI rank. CITED: Local Falcon, AI Overviews proximity whitepaper, ~60,000 simulations.

**Seer Interactive.** Citation analysis. The AI assembles answers by quoting other sources about a business; ChatGPT matches Bing's results 87% of the time.⁶

87%ChatGPT matches Bing's results. CITED: Seer Interactive, SearchGPT/Bing citation & CTR analyses.

**Sensor Tower.** State of AI 2026. The assistant market is fragmenting (ChatGPT 46%, Gemini 28%), yet every assistant grounds answers in retrieved, attested sources the same way.⁷

46%ChatGPT. CITED: Sensor Tower, State of AI 2026.
28%Gemini. CITED: Sensor Tower, State of AI 2026.

**Darren Shaw · Whitespark.** Local Search Ranking Factors 2026. Even the classic local pack is shifting weight toward reviews, third-party attestation, now 16% and rising.⁸

16%Even the classic local pack is shifting weight toward reviews. CITED: Darren Shaw, Whitespark, Local Search Ranking Factors 2026.

**Google + Judge Mehta.** Search Central docs; U.S. v. Google. Robby Stein describes "query fan-out"; court filings disclose FastSearch/RankEmbed, semantic retrieval of entities, not link-counting.⁹,¹²,¹⁷

**Retrieval science.** Peer-reviewed literature. Aggarwal (Princeton), Dai, Fayyaz, Yamada (LUKE): retrievers reward prominent, well-grounded, verifiable entities.¹⁹,²⁵,²⁶,³⁰

**FTC + European Commission.** Consumer Review Rule; EU AI Act. Fabricated attestation is now illegal ($53,088/violation), only genuine signals are durable.³⁵,³⁸

$53,088per violation: fabricated attestation is now illegal. CITED: U.S. FTC, Rule on Consumer Reviews and Testimonials, 16 CFR 465.

**Field reports.** Owners & local SEOs. Businesses surface in AI without buying placement, and mentions lift then decay (Andrew Shotland), exactly as a click-trained retriever predicts.⁴¹

> Eleven instruments, eleven methods, one reading: AI local visibility is won as a verifiable entity, attested consistently across independent sources.

That single substrate is the bird's-eye finding. Everything that follows, the four currents, is simply what this convergence does to a local business, and the one thing the whole landscape is still missing.

## II · Current One, the battlefield left your property

**It's no longer about what you publish**

### In Plain Terms

For twenty years, "doing your SEO" meant working on things you owned: your website, your pages, your Google profile. That era is ending. The things that now make AI recommend you mostly live off your own property, what other people say about you on YouTube, in reviews, in community threads, in local round-ups. You've gone from building your storefront to earning a reputation you don't fully control. The job is no longer to publish more about yourself; it's to be talked about, consistently, by others.

### The Proof

Glenn Allsopp's Ahrefs analysis of 75,000 brands ranked every candidate signal by how strongly it correlates with AI visibility. The signals describing what others say about you, YouTube mentions (0.737), branded web mentions (0.66-0.71), sit at the top. The signals describing what you publish about yourself, your domain rating (0.266), the backlinks you build (0.218), the pages you publish (0.194), sit at the bottom.² The gap is not subtle.

0.66-0.71branded web mentions. CITED: Glenn Allsopp, Ahrefs, AI visibility study, 75,000 brands.
0.266your domain rating. CITED: Glenn Allsopp, Ahrefs, AI visibility study, 75,000 brands.
0.218the backlinks you build. CITED: Glenn Allsopp, Ahrefs, AI visibility study, 75,000 brands.
0.194the pages you publish. CITED: Glenn Allsopp, Ahrefs, AI visibility study, 75,000 brands.

**Figure II · Off-property signals win.** Ahrefs, 75,000 brands (Glenn Allsopp), 2026.

The mechanism, disclosed in Judge Amit Mehta's November 2025 ruling in U.S. v. Google, explains why. Google grounds its Gemini answers through a retriever called FastSearch, built on a deep-learning model, RankEmbed, that matches queries to documents semantically rather than by counting links.¹⁷ Google's own VP of Search, Robby Stein, describes the front end as "query fan-out", the model issues dozens of background searches and synthesizes what it retrieves.¹² Neither process rewards a business for publishing more pages about itself; both reward a business that the wider web independently corroborates. **ANALYSIS** The practical relocation is total: the battlefield moved from your domain to the ecosystem's consensus about you.

## III · Current Two, specificity is rewarded at every layer

**Generic loses; specific wins, everywhere**

### In Plain Terms

The single most repeated pattern across all the evidence is this: the more specific you are, the more AI rewards you, and it shows up at every level. Specific questions get AI answers more often than vague searches. First-hand, specific content beats generic listicles. A review that names exactly what you did ("great with anxious dogs") is worth more than a bare five stars. And a business known for one clear thing beats one that claims to do everything. Being known for the right thing isn't a tagline, it's the rule the whole system runs on.

### The Proof

The same generic-to-specific gradient appears independently at four layers. At the query layer, Ahrefs' study of 146 million SERPs shows single-word searches trigger an AI Overview 9.5% of the time, while full question-style queries trigger 57.9%.³ At the content layer, Google's own Search Central guidance explicitly rewards "non-commodity content" and first-hand experience over generic aggregation.¹⁰ At the review layer, AI answers quote the specific language of reviews verbatim, the named service, not the star count. At the entity layer, the retrieval-science consensus (LUKE-style entity grounding) favors precisely-described, unambiguous entities.³⁰

**Figure III · The specificity ladder.** Query: Ahrefs. Content: Google. Review/entity: platform mechanics & LAIR analysis.

This is the academic and mechanical basis for Local AI Registry's founding principle, alignment, not coverage. **ANALYSIS** A business fails in AI not by being invisible but by being known for the wrong, generic thing. The corrective is specificity, applied deliberately at all four layers at once.

## IV · Current Three, four clocks, one transition window

**Four unrelated timers strike at once**

### In Plain Terms

Four completely separate things are all changing at the same moment, roughly 2026 into 2027. How many people use AI for local search. How open AI is to recommending smaller businesses. How people phrase their searches. And when the new AI transparency laws kick in. None of these has anything to do with the others, which is exactly why their lining up matters. When four unrelated clocks all strike the same hour, that's not coincidence; it's a transition. The businesses that move during the window get an advantage the latecomers won't.

### The Proof

Four independently-measured trends converge on the same window. Adoption: BrightLocal records consumer use of AI for local discovery rising from 6% to 45% across 2025-26.¹ The citation window: Ahrefs finds the share of AI-Overview citations drawn from the organic top ten fell from ~76% to ~38%, widening the pool to the long tail, a window the retrieval-bias literature predicts will re-narrow.⁴,²⁵ The exposure runway: as phrasing turns conversational, local AI-trigger rates climb off their 7.9% floor toward the 57.9% question rate.³ Regulation: the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties take effect 2 August 2026.³⁸

6% to 45%consumer use of AI for local discovery across 2025-26. CITED: BrightLocal, Local Consumer Review Survey 2026.
~76% to ~38%the share of AI-Overview citations drawn from the organic top ten. CITED: Ahrefs, 38% of AI Overview Citations Pull From the Top 10.
7.9%the local AI-trigger rate floor. CITED: Ahrefs, What Triggers AI Overviews? 86 Factors, 146M SERPs.
2 August 2026the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties take effect. CITED: European Commission, EU AI Act, Article 50.

**Figure IV · Four clocks, one transition.** BrightLocal; Ahrefs; European Commission. Convergence framing is analysis. ** PROJECTION**

The convergence itself is the argument. **ANALYSIS** Any one trend could be dismissed as noise; four unrelated research streams agreeing on a transition date is a structural signal that the ground is shifting now, and that early, consistent action dominates a wait-and-see posture.

## V · Current Four, the accountability vacuum

**The Keystone · No one can tell you what the AI says**

### In Plain Terms

Here's the strangest part. Everything above says your AI reputation now matters enormously, but nobody can actually tell you what it is. Ask the same question twice and the AI gives different answers. The platforms don't report which businesses they recommend or why. There's no record that follows you across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google. And the law polices AI that lies to customers, not AI that's wrong about you. So the one thing that now decides whether customers find you is the one thing no one is keeping score of. That gap is the whole reason a registry needs to exist.

### The Proof

Four properties you would expect of any system of record are absent across every major AI surface. Reproducibility: practitioners document that AI Overview results "aren't repeatable" run-to-run, and Google's own Search Console does not separate AI-driven clicks. Accuracy: Nelson Liu and Percy Liang (Stanford) found only 51.5% of generated sentences are fully supported by their citations, and the Tow Center at Columbia found leading AI search tools wrong on more than 60% of queries.³²,³⁴ Cross-platform record: none exists. Regulatory scope: the FTC and EU AI Act target deception of consumers, not accuracy about third-party businesses.³⁵,³⁸

51.5%of generated sentences are fully supported by their citations. CITED: N. F. Liu, T. Zhang, P. Liang (Stanford), Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines.
More than 60%of queries: leading AI search tools wrong. CITED: Tow Center at Columbia, AI Search Has a Citation Problem.

**Figure V · The accountability vacuum.** LAIR analysis of platform reporting, reproducibility & regulatory scope, 2026.

This is the keystone the other three currents rest on. **ANALYSIS** The entire body of evidence converges on "be a verifiable entity," moving fast, on a closing clock, while no neutral party measures whether you are one, reproducibly, across platforms, over time. That negative space, visible only when all eleven streams are held in one frame, is not a gap in the research. It is a description of an institution that does not yet exist.

## VI · The Instrument, what the vacuum implies

If the evidence converges on a substrate no one is measuring, the implied object is not a tactic or a tool, it is an institution: an independent, reproducible record of what AI says about local businesses, and whether they are known for the right things.

That is the function Local AI Registry performs. It scores independent local businesses across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews; it measures not just whether a business is named but whether it is named for the right service, the alignment this report shows the whole system rewards; and it does so repeatedly, across platforms, over time, which is exactly the reproducibility the landscape lacks. The registry is not a product appended to the research. It is the instrument the convergence implies.

### From reading to record

A reader can act on the four currents today: move the work off-property, apply specificity at every layer, act within the window, and treat verifiability as a conversion advantage. But to know where you stand, what you're named for, what you're invisible for, where the reputation and the marketing diverge, requires the instrument. That is what the next page offers.

## VII · The evidence layer, seven findings underneath

**Seven findings underneath the view**

The bird's-eye view is built on a deeper layer of cross-source findings, each one a conclusion drawn by overlaying two or three datasets that none of them states alone. They are summarized here as the supporting evidence beneath the four currents; each is documented at length in companion analysis.

### The seven triangulated findings beneath the convergence

- **01 · The Broken Scoreboard.** The canonical local-pack model and AI visibility are nearly orthogonal. Built from: Ahrefs × Whitespark × antitrust.
- **02 · The Exposure Runway.** The 7.9% local AI rate is a countdown toward the 57.9% question rate. Built from: Ahrefs × BrightLocal.
- **03 · Re-Centralization.** Proximity's death plus prominence bias tilts AI toward incumbents. Built from: Local Falcon × retrieval-bias research.
- **04 · The Closing Window.** A temporary long-tail citation opening that bias predicts will re-narrow. Built from: Ahrefs × field experiment × academia.
- **05 · Reviews Are the Keystone.** The only lever that is ranking signal, citation source, safeguard & legal moat at once. Built from: Whitespark × mechanism × Liu × FTC.
- **06 · The Verification Dividend.** The fact-check, not the recommendation, is where the funnel breaks. Built from: BrightLocal × Tow Center.
- **07 · Two Disjoint Games.** ChatGPT-via-Bing visibility is the underpriced channel. Built from: Seer × Ahrefs × Sensor Tower.

Each finding is graded **ANALYSIS**, a strong hypothesis from real, cited inputs, not a measured fact. Several become measurable original statistics when cross-checked against the live index; those measurements will be published when complete.

## Methodology & limitations

### How this report was built

This is a work of synthesis at altitude: eleven independent evidence streams, read together to surface the conclusions that only their overlap reveals. Every input is a real, cited figure from a named source; the convergence and the four currents are our own **ANALYSIS**; forward inferences are marked ** PROJECTION**. We hold a strict "real or omitted" rule, no quote, statistic, study, court finding, or researcher is invented, and unverifiable figures (such as a widely-shared "797,444 impressions, 7 clicks" anecdote) are excluded rather than repeated.

### What this method can and cannot claim

Convergence is strong evidence, not proof of mechanism. Many independent sources agreeing on a substrate is a powerful signal, but several inputs are correlational and inherit that limit. Projections are reasoned, not certain, the transition window and the runway are extrapolations from measured trends, flagged as such. The local-AI research gap is real: little peer-reviewed work studies local-business inclusion in AI answers directly, so local conclusions are careful inferences from adjacent retrieval, bias, and entity-grounding research. Vendor incentive exists in some sources; figures were cross-checked where possible. The accountability vacuum is, by definition, where measurement is thinnest, which is precisely the gap the registry is built to close, and why proprietary figures are shown as forthcoming rather than asserted.

Reference numbers are shared across the Local AI Visibility Series for cross-referencing; gaps indicate sources cited in companion papers.

# How AI sends customers through the door

> Original AEO research from Local AI Registry on how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity find and recommend local businesses.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/research/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Find any business on the map

Every day people ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google where to go. We study how those answers are made, and which local businesses they name.

[Explore the research ↓](#library)
