# Privacy Policy

> How Local AI Registry collects, uses, and protects information about you and the businesses we serve, including data accessed via Google Business Profile.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/legal/privacy/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Legal

Section 01

## Introduction

Local AI Registry is a product of **Blind LLC** (“we,” “our,” or “us”). When we say “the Services,” we mean our website at localairegistry.com, the owner dashboards it hosts, the public business profile pages we generate, the review-collection and photo-upload tools we host on your behalf, and the integrations that connect those tools to Google and the other platforms listed below.

By using the Services, you accept the practices described in this policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the Services. We’ll always tell you when this document materially changes (see Section 14).

Section 02

## Information we collect

### Information you give us directly

When you create an account, claim a business, or buy a plan, you provide your name, email address, phone number, business name and address, the services your business offers, and the keywords you want us to track. If you pay for a plan, your card details go directly to our payment processor, we never store or see full card numbers, CVV codes, or bank details.

### Information from the public web and our partners

For every business we surface on the public site, we collect information from Google Maps, public review platforms, business websites we scrape with permission, and SEO data providers (DataForSEO and others listed in Section 7). This includes hours, categories, photos, opening times, popular times, organic keyword rankings, backlinks, and reviews. We compute a Digital Score from these signals.

### Information from connected accounts

When you authorize a paid plan that includes the Google Business Profile integration, we receive access tokens that let us read and (with your approval) write to your listing on your behalf. See Section 4 for exactly what we do with that access, and how to revoke it at any time.

### Information collected automatically

When you visit the public site or your dashboard, we record limited usage information: your IP address (used briefly for spam protection and rate limiting), browser and device type, the pages you view, and how you arrived. We use this to keep the site fast, fix bugs, and protect against abuse.

We log a salted SHA-256 hash of (IP + 30-minute time bucket) on public profile pageviews so business owners can see how many distinct visitors viewed their profile this week without us storing the raw IP. After the bucket window expires, the hash cannot be reversed.

### Customers your business sends to us

If you use our review collection or photo upload tools, your customers may give us their name, rating, written feedback, and photos via your branded link. We process this on your behalf as your service provider; you remain the controller of that data. We do not contact those customers for any reason other than the flow they entered.

Section 03

## How we use your information

We use the information described in Section 2 to:

- Provide, operate, secure, and improve the Services.
- Compute Digital Scores and editorial summaries for every business listed on the public site.
- Deliver the SEO modules you have purchased, including drafting Google Business Profile posts, replying to reviews, building citations, and producing monthly reports.
- Process payments, manage subscriptions, and prevent fraud.
- Send transactional messages: phone verification codes, approval requests, billing receipts, weekly progress digests, and monthly reports.
- Respond to support requests and dispute resolution.
- Comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms of Service.

We do not sell your personal information. We do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. We do not buy advertising profiles to target you.

Section 04

## Google API Services data

Local AI Registry accesses your Google account data only with your explicit OAuth authorization and only for the purposes you sign up for. **Local AI Registry’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app will adhere to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.**

### Scopes we may request

Depending on the modules you purchase, we request access to the following Google services:

Sign in with Google
:   Basic profile (name, email, profile photo) so you can log in to Local AI Registry with your Google account.

Google Business Profile
:   Read your business listing details, posts, photos, reviews, and Q&A. Write new posts, photos, and review replies on your behalf when you approve them (or pre-approve them via Auto-Approve in Settings).

### How we use Google data

Google account information is used solely to identify you when you sign in. Google Business Profile data is used to populate your owner dashboard, surface what needs attention, draft content for your approval, and publish that content to your listing after you (or your designated approver) approve it. We do not use Google data to train generalized AI/ML models, and we do not transfer Google data to third parties except the sub-processors strictly necessary to operate the Services (Section 7).

### How to revoke access

You can revoke our access to your Google account at any time at [myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions). When you revoke access, any pending automated actions on your Google Business Profile are cancelled within minutes. The associated tokens are deleted from our systems within 24 hours.

Section 05

## AI-generated content

Local AI Registry uses large language models (OpenAI and Google Gemini, principally) to draft Google Business Profile posts, review replies, FAQ answers, monthly report narratives, and content suggestions. These drafts are generated against your business’s data, your selected brand voice, and your written brand rules.

Every AI-generated artifact that publishes to a public platform passes through an approval gate by default. You can pre-approve specific content types under Settings → Auto-Approve, in which case those drafts ship without per-item review, you remain fully responsible for the published output. We log every draft, every approval, and every publish so you can audit the chain end-to-end from your dashboard.

AI providers may briefly cache prompts and responses for safety and abuse-monitoring purposes per their published policies. We do not authorize providers to use your data for model training, and we use API tiers that contractually prohibit such use where available.

Section 06

## Cookies and similar technologies

Local AI Registry uses a small number of essential cookies: a session cookie when you log in, a CSRF protection cookie, and a preference cookie for any dashboard layout choices you make.

We also use two privacy-respecting analytics tools to understand how the site is used: Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity. They tell us which pages people visit, how they arrive, and where the site is slow or confusing. Microsoft Clarity records anonymized session activity, clicks, scrolls, and page navigation, so we can find and fix bugs and rough edges. We use this only to measure and improve the Services. We do not use advertising cookies, we do not sell your information, and we do not track you across other sites for advertising (see Section 3).

Where we use a third party to deliver part of the Services (a hosted Stripe Checkout page, for example), that third party may set its own cookies on its own domain; their cookie policies govern that use.

Section 07

## Third-party processors

We rely on the sub-processors below to operate the Services. Each one receives only the data needed for its specific function, under a data-processing agreement that restricts re-use. You can request a current list at any time by contacting us.

Stripe
:   Payment processing, subscription billing, customer portal. We send Stripe your email, business name, and the modules you bought.

Twilio
:   Phone-number verification (SMS OTP) and outbound transactional SMS. We send Twilio your phone number and the message to deliver.

Resend
:   Transactional email (verification, approval requests, weekly digests, monthly reports). We send Resend recipient email addresses and message contents.

Google (Cloud, Places, Maps, PageSpeed, Business Profile)
:   Sign-in, location autocomplete, map rendering, site performance scoring, GBP read and write. Data flows are scoped per Section 4.

DataForSEO
:   Keyword ranking data, SERP screenshots, organic traffic estimates, backlink data, review ingestion, business listing data. We send DataForSEO public business identifiers (website, name, address, GBP placeId) and target keywords.

BrightLocal
:   Citation campaign management for paid customers on the Off-Page module. We send BrightLocal the business NAP (name, address, phone) and category data.

OpenAI
:   AI-generated content drafting (posts, replies, summaries, reports). We send OpenAI sanitized prompts containing business context, brand voice notes, and content goals. We use API tiers that prohibit training use of submitted data.

Google Gemini
:   AI-generated content drafting and AI visibility checks. Same handling as OpenAI.

SerpZilla / SerpClix / Adsy / RedPress
:   Off-page module vendors used only for customers actively enrolled in those modules: backlinks, CTR campaigns, press release distribution.

DigitalOcean
:   Application hosting, managed Postgres, object storage (DO Spaces) for photos and report PDFs.

Cloudflare
:   CDN, DDoS protection, bot mitigation in front of public routes.

Sentry
:   Error monitoring. Sentry may capture stack traces and request metadata when our application encounters an error. We scrub personally identifying parameters before sending.

No mobile information will be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. Information sharing to subcontractors in support services, such as customer service, is permitted. All other use case categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.

Section 08

## When we disclose your information

We disclose information only in these specific circumstances:

- **To deliver the Services.** The sub-processors in Section 7 receive what they need to do their job and nothing more.
- **With your direction.** If you connect Google, or instruct us to publish content, we transmit the corresponding data to those platforms on your behalf.
- **To comply with law.** We may disclose information when required by a valid subpoena, court order, or government request. We push back where the request is overbroad and notify you where we are legally permitted to do so.
- **To protect rights and safety.** Where necessary to investigate fraud, security incidents, or violations of our Terms of Service.
- **Business transfer.** If Blind LLC is acquired or merged, customer data transfers to the acquirer under the same protections.

Section 09

## Data retention

We keep account data for as long as your account is active, plus a short tail to handle disputes, support, and legal obligations. Specifically:

- **Account profile and business data:** kept while the account is active; deleted within 30 days of account closure (or sooner on request).
- **OAuth tokens (Google):** deleted within 24 hours of revocation or account closure.
- **Pageview hashes (Section 2):** raw IP is never persisted; the salted hash is kept for 13 months for week-over-week trend reporting, then purged.
- **Billing records:** retained for 7 years to meet tax and accounting obligations.
- **Application logs:** 30 days, then purged.
- **Public business profile pages** we generate from the public web persist as long as the underlying business is operational. Owners can flag inaccurate data or request removal, see Section 11.

Section 10

## Data security

We protect data with industry-standard controls: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest in managed Postgres and object storage, encrypted secrets, least-privilege access management, structured access logs, and continuous error monitoring. OAuth tokens are stored encrypted with separate key material. Production database access is restricted to a small set of authorized engineers and audited.

No system is impenetrable, so we maintain an incident-response plan and will notify affected users without undue delay if a breach occurs that materially affects their data.

Section 11

## Your rights and choices

You can:

- **Access** the personal information we hold about you by emailing the address in Section 15.
- **Correct** inaccurate information directly in your dashboard, or by writing to us.
- **Delete** your account and associated personal information at any time from Settings → Account, or by writing to us.
- **Port** your data: request a machine-readable export.
- **Restrict or object** to specific processing.
- **Opt out** of non-essential email communications via the unsubscribe link in any non-transactional email.
- **Revoke** OAuth access at any time through the third-party platform (Section 4).
- **Flag** inaccurate data on a public business profile we generated using the “Report inaccuracy” affordance on the page.

If you are in the United Kingdom or another jurisdiction with similar laws (GDPR, UK GDPR), you additionally have the right to lodge a complaint with your local supervisory authority. If you are a California resident, you have rights under the CCPA / CPRA including the right to know what we collect, the right to delete, the right to correct, and the right not to be discriminated against for exercising your rights. We honor all of these rights regardless of your jurisdiction.

Section 12

## International transfers

Local AI Registry is operated from the United States, and our primary infrastructure is hosted in U.S. data centers. If you are accessing the Services from outside the United States (including the United Kingdom), your information will be transferred to and processed in the United States. We rely on Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent mechanisms with our sub-processors where required.

## Our 90-day guarantee

For clients on a Program that includes the guarantee, Local AI Registry guarantees that your business will be named by the tracked Assistants within 90 days of the Effective date, as defined in your Proposal. In short: named in AI in 90 days. Guaranteed.

**What's covered.** Your Proposal lists your Tracked questions, the Assistants we track and what counts as being named. Tracked questions must be real questions customers ask about your services in your area. They can't include your business name.

**How it's measured.** On day 1 we record what each tracked Assistant says for your Tracked questions. Because AI answers vary, we ask each question repeatedly and report how often you're named, using the method on our methodology page. Your monthly report includes the answers as screenshots. Our reporting is the record for this guarantee.

**Your part.** The guarantee depends on you giving us the access we need (for example, to your Google Business Profile and website), responding to requests and approvals within five business days, and not running conflicting work on the same profiles during the guarantee period. Delays on these may pause the 90-day period; we'll tell you in writing if that happens.

**If we miss it.** If your business isn't named within 90 days and you've met the conditions above, we keep providing the Services at no charge until it is named, unless your Proposal states a different remedy. Send your claim in writing within 14 business days after the 90-day period ends. Cancelling before the 90 days are up ends eligibility.

- **[Press releases](../signals/pr/index.html).** You choose what the news is, we draft the release, and nothing goes to the wire until you have signed it off.
- **[The monthly report](../tour/index.html).** Every thirty days you get a PDF of what was done on your account and what moved, counted from the day you bought rather than from the first of the month.

## Things we will never do

- A business can't buy a better score.
- A specialist can't buy a better track record.
- Private customer information doesn't become public because it might be useful to AI.
- Our own services sit in the same list, under the same rules, with no boost.

## The guardrails built into the work

Trust isn't a badge. It's what the system refuses to do. These rules run on every account:

- **No medical claims.** A scan runs on every draft and on the title. An outcome promise, a recovery time, a typical result or a safety word blocks the draft outright for health-adjacent categories.
- **No described before and after photos.** A photo classified as a result is never described and never published by us. Advertising rules on outcome claims apply to a picture the same way they apply to a sentence.
- **Bad reviews wait for you.** Only if you approve one. A one or two star review is read by our team first, and where a reply is written it is held until it reaches you, so nothing goes up under your name unless you approve it.
- **Press releases wait for your yes.** A press release never goes out unless you approve it. If the deadline passes without you sending it, we cancel the order, tell you we did not buy it, and draft a fresh one on the next round.
- **Nothing buys itself.** Queued, never auto-confirmed. A person on our team confirms every purchase, under a spending limit, so nothing buys itself.
- **A failed check is recorded as a failure.** We record the answer text, the businesses named in it, and where you came in. If a check fails, we record it as a failed check, never as you not being named.
- **A person reads your report first.** Yes. Three days before your date it goes to your assigned expert and two people here as a preview, and it can be corrected or held in that window.

Chapter one

## How finding a business changed.

For twenty years, finding a business meant searching and clicking.

You typed a few words, opened tab after tab, compared reviews, and called around.

Now people just ask. And AI gives one answer.

No list of links. No tabs. One recommendation, said with confidence.

But AI can only recommend what it understands.

And for most local businesses, the facts online don't agree with each other.

Most local businesses are in pieces online.

Their  hours,  prices,  reviews and  licenses live on dozens of sites. Many of them disagree.

And now everyone is building walls.

Websites are locking AI out, charging tolls, or suing each other. Every new wall makes the answers AI gives a little worse.

1. 2023**Publishers take AI to court.** The New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft over its articles.
2. 2024**Data goes behind deals.** Reddit licenses its posts to Google and OpenAI. Most of the web gets no deal at all.
3. 2025**The web blocks AI by default.** Cloudflare starts blocking AI crawlers for new sites unless they pay per crawl.
4. 2025**Stores fight shopping agents.** Amazon sues Perplexity to stop its AI agent from shopping for people.

So AI guesses. Or it picks someone else.

Often the biggest name, not the best one. A great small business can be invisible without ever knowing why.

AI is deciding who to trust right now.

When everyone builds walls, the small business disappears.

Local AI Registry Journal · Vol. 1, No. 1November 2026 · 8 min read

### How Often AI Recommends Your Business: A Better Measure of Local Visibility

Local AI Registry Research · 14 references · 9 peer-reviewed

**Abstract.** A single AI answer is an observation, not a ranking. Across studies of web search, generative search, local audits and medical recommendations, answers to the same question vary from run to run, by place, by wording and over time. We argue that local visibility is best measured as a recommendation frequency under stated conditions, and propose five principles for measuring it.

**Fig. 1** Evidence that answers behave like samples. Each bar is its own metric; values are not comparable across studies.

Businesses "always present" across locations, ChatGPT local searches**3.5%** BrightLocal, 200k local AI searches

Median overlap, same question asked ~39 minutes apart**29%** 8ight.AI, Study 01

Doctors matching a real clinician: without search vs with search**10.8% → 63.9%** Ibrahim and Zaki, 2026 (preprint)

Appropriate recommendations, depending only on how the question was worded**46.6% vs 74.7%** Parikh et al., Cureus 2024

**Fig. 2** One question, asked 20 times. Blue = named. The rate on the right is what we should measure, not any single answer. *Illustration with simulated data.*

**Fig. 3** How sure can you be? 95% interval for a business named 30% of the time, by number of answers sampled. One answer tells you almost nothing. *Illustrative calculation.*

Five principles for measuring AI visibility

1. Report a rate, with its conditions
2. Sample enough answers
3. Separate being named from being first
4. Verify what is counted
5. Tell noise from real change

# Where each AI assistant gets its local business information

> How ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, Copilot, Siri, Alexa, Meta AI and Grok choose which local businesses to recommend.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

By assistant

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Each assistant checks a business against the sources it trusts before naming it. Google's assistants lean on Google's data, Copilot on Bing, and ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude on their own web searches. The shared foundation is consistent facts, strong reviews and outside mentions.

Every assistant finds local businesses a little differently. Some lean on Google's data, some on Bing, some on their own search. The work that gets you recommended is mostly shared, but the priorities change. Pick an assistant to see how it chooses and what to fix first.

[OpenAI

**ChatGPT** Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website.](../ai/chatgpt/index.html)[Google

**Google AI Overviews and AI Mode** Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data.](../ai/google-ai-overviews/index.html)[Google

**Gemini** Gemini can draw on Google Search and Google Maps, so the businesses it recommends usually have complete Google Business Profiles, strong recent reviews and websites that rank for their services.](../ai/gemini/index.html)[Perplexity

**Perplexity** Perplexity searches the web for every answer and shows its sources.](../ai/perplexity/index.html)[Anthropic

**Claude** When Claude searches the web for a local question, it reads and cites public sources: review sites, guides, news and business websites.](../ai/claude/index.html)[Microsoft

**Microsoft Copilot** Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.](../ai/copilot/index.html)[Apple

**Siri and Apple Intelligence** When someone asks Siri for a nearby business, Apple draws on Apple Maps data.](../ai/siri/index.html)[Amazon

**Alexa+** Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web.](../ai/alexa/index.html)[Meta

**Meta AI** Meta AI lives inside Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger and can search the web for local questions.](../ai/meta-ai/index.html)[xAI

**Grok** Grok, xAI's assistant inside X, searches the web and posts on X.](../ai/grok/index.html)

## What every assistant has in common

All of them want to be confident before they name a business. They get that confidence from agreement across sources, which is why the [11 signals](../signals/index.html) apply everywhere. Start with the [complete guide](../guide/index.html), then use the pages above to set priorities for the assistants your customers use.

# How do I get my business recommended by Alexa?

> Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web. Accurate listings on the major directories and review sites, especially the ones that feed voi.

Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Alexa+

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Alexa answers local questions from partner data and the web. Accurate listings on the major directories and review sites, especially the ones that feed voice assistants, give Alexa the details it needs.

## How does Alexa+ choose which local businesses to recommend?

Amazon's newer Alexa+ assistant handles more conversational requests, including finding and booking local services. It relies on partner data sources and listings rather than one public index, which makes consistent, accurate directory data the priority.

New data from our research team

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**1 of 207** local AI answers gave a street address or phone number](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle)[**83.6%** of local AI answers told people to check with their local store](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle)

**1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number.** Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places.Figure 16, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

**AI answers local questions with national facts.** 65.7% of local answers spoke about “all locations” or “most stores” (vs 2.3% of other answers), and 83.6% hedged (vs 2.6%). National facts are the AI’s default for local questions.Figure 15, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png)

# How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?

> Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/chatgpt/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

ChatGPT

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Claim your business in ChatGPT's Business Hub and make sure OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, can read your website. Then give ChatGPT sources that agree: the same name, address, phone and hours everywhere, steady reviews on more than one site, mentions on local best-of lists and articles, and a clear page for every service.

## How do I claim my business in ChatGPT?

OpenAI opened **Business Hub** in November 2026, a free beta where owners claim the profile ChatGPT already keeps for their business. Open Business Hub from the ChatGPT sidebar, search for your business and claim it. You then confirm you own or represent it through one of the routes offered: your business phone, business email, a DNS record on your website's domain, or a Shopify login. OpenAI also asks for an identity check before you can publish changes or see insights.

Once approved you can update your website, description, category, logo and photos, and see 28 days of insights: how often ChatGPT mentioned you, clicks to your site and the topics people found you through. Local businesses in the US claim an existing listing rather than creating a new one.

OpenAI is clear that claiming does not guarantee better placement. It gives you control of the facts you supply. Our step-by-step guide covers every screen: [how to claim your business in ChatGPT](../../guide/claim-your-business-in-chatgpt/index.html). OpenAI's own help article: [Setting up your business on ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001635-setting-up-your-business-on-chatgpt).

What we saw when we asked ChatGPT ourselves

- In New York, ChatGPT put four different surgeons first across six asks of the same question on Nov 13, 2026.
- After its list, ChatGPT asked follow-up questions: the result the person wants, first surgery or revision, and in one run their budget.
- Most entries quoted a RealSelf rating and review count.

[See every screenshot in AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html)

New data from our research team

**29%**

When ChatGPT got the same local question about 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses it named appeared in both answers (8ight.AI, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**3.5%**

Only 3.5% of businesses ChatGPT named in localized searches appeared at every test point across a town (BrightLocal, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

**52.8%**

ChatGPT declined to recommend an orthopedic surgeon in 52.8% of 40,500 persona-based requests (Haupt et al., 2026, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions, and [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html), our screenshots of ChatGPT's answers. Every number links to its chart.

[**2 of 10** US cities got the same #1 surgeon in six ChatGPT asks of one question](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**27 of 30** ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**~35%** of cited sources stayed the same when the same question was worded differently](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording)

**Different wording, different sources, same answer.** Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer.Illustration 5, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

**Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated.Figure 20, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

## Can ChatGPT read my website?

ChatGPT search finds websites with a crawler called **OAI-SearchBot**. OpenAI says sites that block it will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, and that a change to robots.txt takes about 24 hours to apply. Ask whoever runs your website to check that your robots.txt file, firewall and hosting all let it in:

```
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
```

Two other OpenAI crawlers are separate. **GPTBot** collects content that may be used to train OpenAI's models, and you can block it without leaving ChatGPT search. ** ChatGPT-User** visits a page when a person asks ChatGPT to open it. Source: [OpenAI's crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots).

Make sure your pages also load without a login, list your name, address, phone and hours as text (not only in an image), and are in a sitemap.

## How does ChatGPT choose which local businesses to recommend?

For local questions, ChatGPT usually searches the web before answering. It reads a handful of results, including review sites, maps listings, local guides and business websites, then writes a short answer that names a few businesses. When it shows sources, those are the pages that shaped the answer.

OpenAI has not published a full list of the data providers behind its local results, so the practical approach is to be strong in the places it is seen to cite: review platforms, local best-of lists, news and your own site.

## What did ChatGPT say when we asked it 16 local questions?

On Nov 13, 2026 our research team asked ChatGPT 16 local questions, three times each, and screenshotted every answer. The table counts how many different businesses came back across the three asks, and how many were named every single time.

| Question | Different names | Named all 3 times |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “best Botox injector in Newport Beach” | 10 | 0 |
| “best aesthetic clinic in Beaconsfield” | 5 | 3 |
| “best aesthetic clinic in London” | 10 | 1 |
| “best breast augmentation surgeon in NYC” | 7 | 3 |
| “best closed rhinoplasty surgeon in Los Angeles” | 6 | 3 |
| “best lip filler in Newport Beach” | 9 | 1 |
| “best plastic surgeon in New York City” | 12 | 1 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Atlanta” | 7 | 3 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Chicago” | 6 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Dallas” | 7 | 1 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Houston” | 6 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Miami” | 5 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in New York” | 13 | 0 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Phoenix” | 7 | 4 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in San Diego” | 6 | 3 |
| “best rhinoplasty surgeon in Scottsdale” | 6 | 3 |

Two patterns stand out. In crowded markets like New York, ChatGPT gave a different shortlist almost every time: 13 different names for one rhinoplasty question, and nobody made all three lists. In smaller markets the shortlist was steadier. So being named once proves very little. What matters is how often you're named across many asks, which is exactly what we measure for clients. ## Frequently asked questions

Can I pay ChatGPT to recommend my business?

No. ChatGPT now shows some ads, labeled and kept separate from its answers, and OpenAI says advertising does not influence ChatGPT's own recommendations. Claiming your Business Hub profile is free and does not buy placement either.

Do I have to allow GPTBot to show up in ChatGPT?

No. GPTBot is OpenAI's training crawler. Showing up in ChatGPT search depends on OAI-SearchBot, which you can allow on its own.

Why does ChatGPT give different businesses each time?

Answers vary with wording, location and the sources it happens to read. Businesses that are strong across many sources show up most consistently.

# How do I get my business to show up in Microsoft Copilot?

> Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/copilot/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Microsoft Copilot

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Copilot draws on Bing search, so an accurate Bing Places listing, consistent directory details, reviews and a website that ranks in Bing are the foundation.

## How does Microsoft Copilot choose which local businesses to recommend?

Copilot is Microsoft's assistant across Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft 365. Its web answers are grounded in Bing search results, which means your Bing presence matters more here than anywhere else.

New data from our research team

**63.9%**

Walmart ranked in 11 of 15 answers and was cited once.Figure 10, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews.png)

# How do I get my business recommended by Gemini?

> Gemini can draw on Google Search and Google Maps, so the businesses it recommends usually have complete Google Business Profiles, strong recent reviews and.

Gemini

# How do I get my business into Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode?

> Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/ai/google-ai-overviews/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Google AI Overviews and AI Mode

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Google's AI answers are built on Google Search and Google's local data. A complete, active Google Business Profile, strong reviews, pages that rank for your services and clear structured data on your website are the foundation.

## How does Google AI Overviews and AI Mode choose which local businesses to recommend?

AI Overviews appear above regular Google results, and AI Mode is a full conversational search. For local questions both draw on Google's search index and its local business data, the same information behind Google Maps. Google publishes guidance that the same practices behind good search results apply to its AI features.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**67.5%**

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**76.4%** of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category)[**67.5%** of citations in local AI answers came from news coverage](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration)[**1.0%** of citations went to the business itself for generic “what's open” questions](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap)[**7.2** sources cited per local AI answer, versus 8.1 for other topics](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#sources-per-ai-overview-answer-distribution)

**Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.Figure 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**Local searches got an AI answer 76% of the time, even more often than other questions.** Controlling for phrasing, local searches were still 12 points more likely to get an AI Overview than other question-style searches (76.4% vs 64.1%).Figure 4, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png)

**How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business.** For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store.Illustration 2, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

**The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited.** Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places.Figure 9, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.png)

## What did 7,583 Google AI answers show?

For [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our research team pulled thousands of Google AI answers to local questions and read every source each one cited. Here is what Google's AI did with local businesses:

| Finding | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic | 76.4% |
| Of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites | 6.5% |
| Of citations in local AI answers came from news coverage | 67.5% |
| Of local AI answers told people to check with their local store | 83.6% |
| Local AI answers gave a street address or phone number | 1 of 207 |
| Sources cited per local AI answer, versus 8.1 for other topics | 7.2 |
| Of local AI claims were supported by the pages the AI cited | 87.8% |
| Of business-site citations came from beyond Google's first page | 4.1% |
| More likely: local TV station sites cited in local answers vs other answers | 18x |

Put simply: Google's AI shows up on most local searches, it rarely quotes the business's own website, and it leans on news and other outside sources. It also tells people to check with the store far more often than it gives them an address. The business that wins is the one other sites describe clearly and consistently.

Siri and Apple Intelligence

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** When someone asks Siri for a nearby business, Apple draws on Apple Maps data. Claim your free Apple Business Connect listing, keep it accurate and complete, and make sure your reviews and details match everywhere else.

## How does Siri and Apple Intelligence choose which local businesses to recommend?

Siri answers local questions using Apple Maps information, and Apple Intelligence brings more assistant features to iPhone. Apple Business Connect is the free tool that lets you control how your business appears in Maps, Siri and other Apple apps.

New data from our research team

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks). [Local AI Registry data](../../methodology/index.html)

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**1 of 207** local AI answers gave a street address or phone number](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle)[**83.6%** of local AI answers told people to check with their local store](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle)

**1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number.** Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places.Figure 16, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

**One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.Illustration 6, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

## Do you track Siri and Apple Intelligence?

Our monthly check covers ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini today, the assistants most people use to find a local business. Siri and Apple Intelligence isn't in the monthly check yet. The good news: the work that gets you named by one assistant carries over to the others, because they all read the same kinds of sources. A business that's consistent, reviewed and written about is easier for every assistant to recommend.

## What should I fix first for Siri and Apple Intelligence?

These signals carry the most weight for Siri and Apple Intelligence, in order:

01

**[Directory listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)**  
Same name, address, phone and hours everywhere.

02

**[Reviews](../../signals/reputation/index.html)**  
Reviews, ratings and replies across sites.

03

**[Photos](../../signals/photo-codifying/index.html)**  
Photos labeled so AI can read what they show.

04

**[Google profile](../../signals/google-profile/index.html)**  
Complete, active and posting every week.

05

**[Website](../../signals/web-management/index.html)**  
A fast site with the code AI reads.

# Same question. Different answer.

> We asked ChatGPT the same question six times in 10 cities and screenshotted every answer. Dated, unedited receipts of who AI recommends, and how often.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/answer-watch/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

AI Answer Watch

By [Steve Lee](../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

We ask AI the questions real customers ask, the same way they ask them, and screenshot every answer. Then we ask again. This page is the receipt: dated, unedited and repeatable.

Three asks. Three different top fives.

| Amy Hsu | 1 of 3 | #3 |
| Paul Nassif | 1 of 3 | #4 |

## What we noticed

- **No two answers matched.** Eight different surgeons appeared across three runs of the same question. Only two were named every time.
- **Position moves.** The same surgeon was #1 in one run and #3 in the next. A single screenshot is a snapshot, not a ranking.
- **RealSelf shows up everywhere.** Most entries quoted a RealSelf rating and review count, often as the only source shown.
- **ChatGPT interviews the patient.** After the list, it asked about the result they want, first surgery or revision, and in one run their budget.

That's why we measure how often AI names a business across repeated asks, not where it lands once. It's the same way every client's AI Score is measured.

- **Review count didn't decide the order.** The #1 roofer had 40 reviews; the #3 had 229. The LASIK practice with 895 reviews and a 5.0 rating came fourth.
- **Photos came from anywhere.** Pictures beside named businesses came from directories, a used-truck listing and other companies' websites.
- **The rating in the answer wasn't always the rating on the map.** For three car dealers, ChatGPT quoted a higher Birdeye or DealerRater rating than the Google rating on its own map.
- **Few links.** Facts came from map listings. The pages it linked were mostly licensing boards and best-of lists.

## Method and disclosure

Each run was a new temporary chat with personalization turned off, typed exactly as shown. Screenshots are cropped only to remove the account sidebar and empty margins. Each shows the top of the answer; the full ordered list from the same moment is printed under it. Tests 05 and 06 were captured Nov 15, 2026 through DataForSEO: ChatGPT's web answer with web search on, asked from the United States, and Claude, Gemini and Perplexity through their APIs with web search on; each question was asked once. Tests 02 to 04 were captured Nov 13, 2026, between 3:30 and 5:08 PM PT. In Test 02, Los Angeles' first three asks are the Test 01 runs. Where ChatGPT spelled one surgeon's name two ways, we count it once. Times are Pacific. Dr. Deepak Dugar is a Local AI Registry client; we report him the same way as everyone else.

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**6.5%** of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap)[**~35%** of cited sources stayed the same when the same question was worded differently](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording)[**76.4%** of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category)

**One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.Illustration 6, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

**Local AEO priority map: what AI cites vs what you control.** The sources AI cites most for local answers (news) are the ones businesses control least, and the source they fully control (their site) is cited least. AEO closes that gap from both sides.Figure 23, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#local-aeo-priority-2x2-control-vs-citation-share), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-aeo-priority-2x2-control-vs-citation-share.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/local-aeo-priority-2x2-control-vs-citation-share.png)

# Local AI Registry vs Birdeye

> Local AI Registry vs Birdeye: what each does, who each is best for and how they differ for getting a local business named in AI answers.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/compare/birdeye/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Comparison

Birdeye is reputation and customer experience software for local businesses: reviews, listings, messaging and surveys, with newer AI search visibility features. Local AI Registry is a done-for-you program that gets local businesses named in AI answers, built on a public, verified record. Here's an honest look at how they differ.

## At a glance

|  | Birdeye | Local AI Registry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you get | Software for reviews, listings, messaging and surveys. | A done-for-you team focused on getting you named in AI answers. |
| Who does the work | Your staff, inside the app. | Our team. You review everything first. |
| Press, best-of guides and video | Not the core of the platform. | Included in the work. |
| Original research | Not the focus. | Our research team publishes original studies on how AI picks local businesses. |
| Guarantee | Software subscription. | Named in AI in 90 days. Guaranteed. |

## Who Birdeye is best for

Businesses that want an all-in-one review and messaging tool their staff manages day to day.

## Who Local AI Registry is best for

Owners who want to be the business AI names when someone nearby asks, without learning another tool or managing another vendor. One team does the work and shows you the proof every month.

## What Birdeye does well

- Review requests by text and email, so happy customers actually leave reviews.
- One inbox for messages from Google, Facebook, text and webchat.
- Surveys and customer experience reporting for staff to act on.

# Data Policy: What We Hold and Why

> What Local AI Registry records about a local business, where it comes from, and how to correct it or opt out.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/data-policy/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Data policy

Data policy

## What we hold, and why.

We keep a public record of how AI assistants describe local businesses. Here’s what that record holds, where it comes from, and what you can do about yours.

01

## What we record

For each business: the public facts, name, address, category, hours, website, public contact details, alongside what AI assistants say when asked to recommend a business like it, a summary of public reviews and ratings, and the AI Score we calculate from all of it.
02

## Where it comes from

Public sources only: the open web, business listings, mapping providers, and the answers we get by putting real questions to AI assistants. We don’t buy private data, and we don’t track individual people.
03

## How the score is built

One method, applied the same way to every business, eight signals, documented weights, no paid placement. A business can’t buy a better score. [Read the method](../methodology/index.html)
04

## Public vs. private

A profile is public, that’s the point of a registry. Account details for owners who register (login, billing, internal notes) are private, used only to run the service, and never sold.
05

## How long we keep it

We keep a profile current and re-score it periodically, so it shows what AI says now and not what it said a year ago. Remove a business and we stop maintaining its profile.

Your choices

Still have a question? [Get in touch](../contact/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**76.4%** of local business searches showed a Google AI answer, more than any other topic](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category)[**1.0%** of citations went to the business itself for generic “what's open” questions](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap)[**6.5%** of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap)

**Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.Figure 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited.** Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places.Figure 9, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.png)

# AI visibility for cannabis dispensaries

> When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near them, we work to have you in the answer. Free AI Score, then the work that moves it.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/for/cannabis-dispensaries/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Dispensaries

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Dispensaries are locked out of most paid channels, which makes being named in an answer worth more here than in any other trade on this list.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a dispensary near you, you're in the answer.

## What dispensaries are up against

Google Ads will not take you. Meta will not take you. What is left is the organic answer, and the organic answer is increasingly one an assistant writes.

People ask by landmark and by neighborhood far more than they ask by city. Almost every high-volume question we hold in this trade names a park, a station or a mall.

People also do not say "cannabis dispensary". They say dispo, or here, or nothing at all, and the questions we ask on your behalf are asked in those words.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What people ask AI about dispensaries

These are the questions people put to ChatGPT, Gemini and Google about dispensaries, ranked by how often they're searched. None of them names a business. The assistant decides who to name.

| The question | Searches a year |
| --- | --- |
| Where can I find a cannabis dispensary near me? | 4,860 |
| Where is the nearest dispensary? | 4,860 |
| Where can I find the nearest dispensary? | 4,860 |
| What types of cannabis products are available in Chicago dispensaries? | Not measured |
| Which dispensary has the best selection of edibles? | Not measured |

Questions are real rows from Local AI Registry's production demand data, as businesses in this industry asked them. The yearly figure is Google's ask volume for the keyword behind each question. Where a question named a town, the town was taken out.

## What we do for dispensaries

The work that matters most here, and the feature page that explains each one in full.

### [Directory listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

The twenty three general hosts, checked and ordered, so a near-me answer has more than one record of you to assemble from.

### [Review replies](../../signals/reputation/index.html)

A new three star and up review gets a reply drafted in your voice for approval. A low-star review is flagged with a policy read on it, and any reply to one waits for your approval.

### [AI capture](../../signals/ai-monitoring/index.html)

Your questions asked monthly with the screenshots kept, which is the only evidence available in a channel with no ad platform to report on.

From our data · 3D

## What people ask AI about dispensaries

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for dispensaries

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Your trade adds its own on top. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

1. **Week 1: the baseline** We ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions above, anchored to your town, and keep the screenshots. You see who is named today, and whether you are.
2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.
3. **Every week: the work** Posts, review replies and photos go to your approval queue. Nothing goes live without your OK.
4. **Day 90: the check** If AI isn't naming you, we keep working free until it does.

## Frequently asked questions

Will the assistants answer cannabis questions at all?

They do, and we keep the screenshot each time. Where one declines, that is recorded as what happened rather than smoothed over.

We have several stores. Does each one need its own entry?

Yes. A listing is one location, and the near-me answer is decided per location. Each store is its own registry entry.

Dermatology

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a dermatologist near you, you're in the answer.

## What dermatology practices are up against

Dermatology is medical and cosmetic at once. The same practice is asked about skin cancer treatment and laser hair removal, and the two questions reach it through different pages.

Health content is held to a higher bar by Google and by advertising law. That is a constraint on what may be written for you, and we treat it as one.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for dermatology practices

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Because AI reads you as a medical practice, your roster grows to 40, adding Zocdoc, Healthgrades, WebMD, RealSelf, Vitals and more. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

1. **Week 1: the baseline** We ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions above, anchored to your town, and keep the screenshots. You see who is named today, and whether you are.
2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.
3. **Every week: the work** Posts, review replies and photos go to your approval queue. Nothing goes live without your OK.
4. **Day 90: the check** If AI isn't naming you, we keep working free until it does.

## Frequently asked questions

We are a multi-doctor practice. Does each doctor get a page?

The registry entry is the practice. Credentials for individual doctors are facts you supply, and they go on your listing rather than being written by us.

Can you say we are board certified?

Only if you have given us the certification. A credential we do not hold on file is the one thing we will never approximate.

Insurance is the second question, every time. A listing that does not say which plans it takes loses the answer to one that does.

### [Directory listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

Zocdoc, Healthgrades, Vitals and the general set are checked and ordered. Insurance-shaped questions are answered off directory records as often as off your own site.

### [Posts](../../signals/google-profile/index.html)

A post that says what an exam involves and how long it takes answers the third question on the list above, on the page an assistant reads first.

From our data · 3D

## What people ask AI about eye care practices

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for eye care practices

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Because AI reads you as a medical practice, your roster grows to 40, adding Zocdoc, Healthgrades, WebMD, RealSelf, Vitals and more. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

1. **Week 1: the baseline** We ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions above, anchored to your town, and keep the screenshots. You see who is named today, and whether you are.
2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.
3. **Every week: the work** Posts, review replies and photos go to your approval queue. Nothing goes live without your OK.
4. **Day 90: the check** If AI isn't naming you, we keep working free until it does.

## Rules med spas need to follow

Name your medical director and licensed injectors with their credentials; trust signals matter more in medical aesthetics than almost anywhere. Follow your state's rules on who can perform each treatment, and get written consent before posting any before and after photo. Use brand names like Botox correctly and avoid promising results.

## Doing it yourself? Start here

## Frequently asked questions

Should I list prices on my website?

Where you can, yes. Price is one of the most common questions clients ask AI. A clear starting price or range helps assistants answer with your business in mind.

Do before and after photos help with AI?

They help clients more than machines. Label them clearly, follow consent rules and place them on the page for that treatment.

How long does it take for a med spa to show up in AI?

It depends on where you start and how competitive your area is. Fixes to your facts and profile can show up within weeks; reviews, lists and articles build over months. Our [90-day guarantee](../../../guarantee/index.html) reflects that timeline.

Medical clinics

**Short answer** When someone asks ChatGPT for a medical clinic near you, you're in the answer. We get you there by making your business easy for AI to confirm: consistent listings, an active Google profile, reviews with replies, and coverage on other sites.

Most people asking an assistant for a clinic are asking about today: who is open, who is near, who takes their insurance. Hours and address decide more of these answers than anything you write.

**The goal:** When someone asks ChatGPT for a medical clinic near you, you're in the answer.

## What medical clinics are up against

The heaviest demand a clinic sits under is urgent, and it is asked in urgent-care words rather than clinic words. A clinic that does walk-ins and does not say so loses those answers to a business that does.

Hours that disagree between your listing and your site are the single most common gap we find, and it is the cheapest one to close.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What we do for medical clinics

The work that matters most here, and the feature page that explains each one in full.

### [Directory listings](../../signals/directory-listings/index.html)

One record pushed everywhere, so the phone number and the address read the same on every directory an answer might be assembled from.

### [Posts](../../signals/google-profile/index.html)

Posts that state the services, the hours and whether you take walk-ins, on the page an assistant reads first.

### [Review replies](../../signals/reputation/index.html)

A new three star and up review gets a reply drafted for your approval. A one or two star review is flagged to you with a policy read on it, and any reply to one waits for your approval.

## What people ask AI about medical clinics

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), Local AI Registry research, 2026.

Two things follow. First, consistent listings are the floor, not the ceiling: almost no answer repeats your address or phone, so a listings tool alone can't put you in the answer. Second, the sources shift when a question is worded differently, so you need to watch many phrasings every month, not one keyword. In our own [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html) screenshots, 27 of 30 ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources, which is why industry review sites matter so much in medical aesthetics.

## The directories that matter for medical clinics

Every business gets checked on 23 general directories: Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, the BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Nextdoor, Trustpilot and the rest. Because AI reads you as a medical practice, your roster grows to 40, adding Zocdoc, Healthgrades, WebMD, RealSelf, Vitals and more. A directory where we can't find you is recorded as not found, which is a different fact from not listed, and every reading is retired after 30 days so you never see a stale number.

## Your first 90 days

1. **Week 1: the baseline** We ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the questions above, anchored to your town, and keep the screenshots. You see who is named today, and whether you are.
2. **Weeks 1 to 4: the record** You confirm your facts once. We fix your Google profile, audit your directories and order the missing ones.
3. **Every week: the work** Posts, review replies and photos go to your approval queue. Nothing goes live without your OK.
4. **Day 90: the check** If AI isn't naming you, we keep working free until it does.

## Frequently asked questions

We are a clinic, not urgent care. Does that matter?

It matters for what we write. The demand is worded as urgent care and your listing should say plainly what you do and do not do, rather than borrowing a word that would misdescribe you.

How quickly do hours changes reach the assistants?

Your listing updates immediately. What an assistant says catches up on its own schedule, which is why we re-ask your questions every month and show you the answer.

## Questions surgeons ask us

How does ChatGPT decide which plastic surgeons to recommend?

It recommends surgeons it can verify. That means the same facts on Google, directories and review sites, a board certification it can confirm, procedures it can match to the question, and recent reviews. When those sources disagree or say little, it leaves you out.

Is this different from regular SEO?

Yes. SEO gets your website ranked in a list of links. AI search reads many sources at once and names only a few surgeons. You need both. We focus on the part most agencies miss: what AI reads about you away from your own website.

Will this work with my current marketing agency?

Yes. We do not replace your website, ads or social media. We handle the listings, reviews, credentials and monthly AI checks that agencies usually leave alone, and we are happy to share our reports with your agency.

How do you keep review replies HIPAA-safe?

Our replies never confirm that someone is a patient and never mention a procedure or any health details. Every reply lands in your inbox before it goes out, and you have three business days to change it or stop it.

Which AI tools do you track?

ChatGPT, Google Gemini and AI Overviews, Claude and Perplexity. Your monthly report shows what each one says about your practice and what changed.

How long until AI starts naming my practice?

Our goal is about 3 months, and some practices see changes sooner. If AI is not naming you in 90 days, we keep working for free until it does.

**Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.Figure 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited.** Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places.Figure 9, [The Local Answer Gap](../../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.png)

**One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record.Illustration 6, [The Local Answer Gap](../../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../../research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

## Why AI matters for plastic surgeons

Patients choosing a surgeon research for weeks and increasingly ask AI to compare credentials, results and reviews. An assistant that can't confirm board certification or find independent coverage will name someone else.

## Rules plastic surgeons need to follow

State board certification exactly as the certifying board names it, and link to the board's lookup where possible. Follow advertising rules for medical professionals in your state and keep patient privacy rules in mind in every review reply. Never confirm in public that someone is a patient.

## Frequently asked questions

Does a surgeon's personal profile matter?

Yes. Patients often ask about the surgeon by name. A strong individual profile, linked to the practice, helps AI connect the two.

Can I reply to reviews without breaking privacy rules?

Yes, with general replies that don't confirm treatment or share details. When in doubt, take it offline.

How long does it take for a plastic surgery practice to show up in AI?

It depends on where you start and how competitive your area is. Fixes to your facts and profile can show up within weeks; reviews, lists and articles build over months. Our [90-day guarantee](../../../guarantee/index.html) reflects that timeline.
