# How do reviews affect whether AI recommends my business?

> Reviews are one of the main things assistants use to decide who to recommend.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/reputation/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 06 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Reviews are one of the main things assistants use to decide who to recommend. They look at your rating, how many reviews you have, how recent they are, what customers say in their own words, and whether you reply. Reviews on several sites count more than reviews on one.

## What AI reads in your reviews

An assistant doesn't just see a star rating. It reads review text to learn what you're known for. If customers often mention a service, a staff member or a quality like "on time" or "explained everything", the assistant can repeat that when someone asks for exactly that.

What the screenshots show

- RealSelf appeared among the sources of 27 of 30 full “best rhinoplasty surgeon in [city]” answers we screenshotted across 10 cities on Nov 13, 2026.
- In our Los Angeles runs, a RealSelf rating and review count sat right next to most names ChatGPT recommended.

[See every screenshot in AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html)

New data from our research team

**88%**

45% of consumers now use AI for local discovery, up from 6%, and 88% fact-check the result (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey 2026, cited in The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions, and [AI Answer Watch](../../answer-watch/index.html), our screenshots of ChatGPT's answers. Every number links to its chart.

[**27 of 30** ChatGPT answers we screenshotted listed RealSelf among their sources](../../answer-watch/index.html)[**8 words** readable on the median social post Google's AI cited](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source)[**2 of 10** US cities got the same #1 surgeon in six ChatGPT asks of one question](../../answer-watch/index.html)

**Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read.** News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin.Figure 18, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

**Social posts the AI cited had a median of 8 readable words.** The median cited social post had 8 readable words. Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18.Figure 19, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.png)

## What we do for you

We draft a reply to each new three, four and five star review on your Google listing, and you edit, approve or decline it. A reply to a one or two star review is read by our team first, and nothing goes up under your name unless you approve it.

A reply answers the person, not the room. The first sentence responds to what this reviewer said and names what the visit was for. It adds one thing a stranger reading before booking would want, and stops.

A one or two star review is never answered without your approval, at any age. It is flagged to you on your reviews page with what it says, whether it breaks a Google policy and where the removal petition stands. One that lands while you are with us also emails you within hours; one already sitting on the listing when you arrived is flagged without the mail, because a notice about a review from 2019 reads as news and is not.

Thin replies already on your listing are rewritten, up to twenty of them, and never the one under a one or two star review. Four words of thanks under a review that named a treatment is a wasted paragraph on a page an assistant reads.

### What you get

- A drafted reply per unanswered three, four or five star review, newest first.
- A flag on your reviews page for each low-star review, and an email within hours for one less than a fortnight old, with the petition state stated plainly and never overstated.
- The three steps to report a review from your own Google account, because some of them are yours to file and not ours.
- Replies published on your listing under your name.

### How it runs

1. **Reviews are read** The review pass runs every three hours against your Google listing.
2. **Three stars and up are drafted** At most twenty drafts in a run, and at most five a day for reviews older than six months, so a back catalogue is worked through rather than dumped.
3. **One and two stars are pursued** Each one from the last six months is read against Google policy and gets a petition written and assigned to one of our people, because Google only accepts these from a person, so one of our team submits it by hand.
4. **You approve or leave it** Replies to three, four and five star reviews are in the default set that publishes after three business days if untouched. Switch the type to manual and nothing moves without you.

**Why it moves the AI answer** Reviews are the text an assistant quotes when it explains why it picked somebody, and a reply is the only part of that text you get to write.

## What helps most

- A steady flow of new reviews, not a burst once a year.
- Reviews on more than one site: Google plus the review sites your industry uses.
- Customers naming the service they came for.
- A short, personal reply to every review, good or bad.

# Is SEO still needed if customers use AI instead of Google?

> Yes. Many assistants search the web before they answer, and they lean on the pages that already rank well.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/seo/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 04 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Yes. Many assistants search the web before they answer, and they lean on the pages that already rank well. Google's own AI answers are built on Google search results. Strong SEO is often how a page becomes a source for AI in the first place.

## How SEO and AI connect

When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity a local question, the assistant often runs a web search behind the scenes, reads the top results and writes an answer from them. If your pages don't show up in those searches, the assistant may never read them. That is why [AI visibility and SEO](../../signals/seo/index.html) overlap so much: SEO gets you into the reading list, AI visibility gets you into the answer.

New data from our research team

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**147 vs 70** times a store's own site ranked on page one, vs times the AI cited it, across 157 brand questions](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews)[**4.1%** of business-site citations came from beyond Google's first page](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source)[**6.5%** of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap)

**SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.** Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links.Illustration 1, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

**Ranked first, still skipped: why SEO alone isn’t AEO.** In 147 of 157 brand questions the store’s own site ranked on page one, but the AI cited it in only 70. Ranking and being used by AI are separate outcomes.Illustration 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.png)

**Ranked and used vs ranked and ignored: a 2x2 of brand websites.** Most brands ranked on page one nearly every time. What split them was use: Publix, Trader Joe’s and Sam’s Club were cited every time; Walmart, Starbucks and Chipotle were ranked but ignored.Figure 11, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-rank-vs-ai-citation-2x2.png)

## What we do for you

We work on the search rankings that sit under every AI answer: your service pages, the links pointing at them and the technical fixes that let assistants find and cite you.

- A page for each service you want to win, written from your own facts
- Technical fixes that stop crawlers and assistants from missing pages
- Every change dated in your monthly report

## What matters most for a local business

- One page per main service, written in the words customers use.
- A page for each location, with its address, hours and map.
- Answers to real questions near the top of each page.
- Fast pages that work well on a phone.
- Links from other local and industry sites.

## Where SEO stops

Ranking is not the same as being recommended. An assistant can read your top-ranking page and still name a competitor with better [reviews](../../signals/reputation/index.html) or more [outside mentions](../../signals/third-party-articles/index.html). SEO is one signal of eleven.

# Why do articles on other websites matter for AI visibility?

> Assistants trust what independent sites say about you more than what you say about yourself.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/third-party-articles/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 09 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Assistants trust what independent sites say about you more than what you say about yourself. Articles, interviews, guides and partner pages that name your business give AI outside confirmation of who you are and what you're good at.

## Outside proof

When an assistant builds an answer, it pulls from several sources and favors ones that agree. If a local magazine, a partner's blog and an industry guide all describe you the same way, that description becomes the one AI repeats.

New data from our research team

**0.737**

In a 75,000-brand study, the top correlate of AI visibility was YouTube and branded web mentions (0.737), not links or pages (Ahrefs, cited in our white paper The Convergence). [The Convergence](../../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

# What does my website need so AI can understand it?

> Your site needs to load fast, work on a phone, state plainly what you do and where, and include structured data (schema) that labels your business, service.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/signals/web-management/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

What we handle · 05 of 11

By [Steve Lee](../../team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry · Updated November 15, 2026

**Short answer** Your site needs to load fast, work on a phone, state plainly what you do and where, and include structured data (schema) that labels your business, services, hours and reviews in a format machines read without guessing.

## What AI needs from your site

Assistants and search crawlers read your site's code, not its design. They need clear facts: who you are, what services you offer, where, when you're open and how to book. Structured data, often called [schema markup](../../glossary/index.html#schema-markup), states those facts in a standard format so there's nothing to guess.

New data from our research team

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**51.6%**

For claims AI attributed to a store locator, app or official site, 51.6% were not supported by any page it cited. [The Local Answer Gap, LAIR-R-2026-001](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief). [How Often AI Recommends Your Business, LAIR-R-2026-002](../../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html)

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

[**51.6%** of claims citing a store locator or official site had no supporting page](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate)[**6.5%** of the sources Google's AI cited for local questions were the businesses' own websites](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap)[**8 words** readable on the median social post Google's AI cited](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source)

**What Google’s AI can actually read on a page.** News pages the AI cited had about 500 readable words. Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words.Illustration 4, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

**Social posts the AI cited had a median of 8 readable words.** The median cited social post had 8 readable words. Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18.Figure 19, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.png)

**When Google’s AI says “the store locator says,” half the time it can’t show it.** 16 of 31 local claims that cited a store locator, app or official site (51.6%) were not supported by any page the AI cited, against 6.7% of other local claims.Figure 17, [The Local Answer Gap](../../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.svg) · [PNG](../../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.png)

## What we do for you

We keep your website accurate and readable for AI: service pages, schema markup, speed and mobile fixes. If a web team or studio already runs your site, we work alongside them instead of replacing them.

- Service and FAQ schema on the pages that matter
- Hours, prices and team kept in step with your verified record
- Speed and mobile fixes, listed in your monthly report

## The checklist

- Pages load quickly on a phone.
- Every service has its own page with a plain description.
- LocalBusiness schema with name, address, phone, hours and geo-coordinates.
- Service and FAQ schema where they fit.
- No important text hidden inside images or behind clicks.
- An [llms.txt](../../glossary/index.html#llms-txt) file that points AI to your key pages (optional, low effort).

## Free tools to start

Our [schema generator](../../tools/schema-generator/index.html) builds LocalBusiness markup you can paste into your site, and the [llms.txt generator](../../tools/llms-txt-generator/index.html) builds the file in a minute.

# Local AI search statistics, 2026

> Local AI search statistics for 2026: how often AI names local businesses, where AI gets its answers and how answers change, each figure linked to its source.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/statistics/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Statistics

Every number on this page comes from Local AI Registry's own research or from studies our research team reviewed, with the source linked under each one. Cite freely, and link back to the study.

## From our own clients

What we see across the practices we manage.

**15%** of new clients are named by ChatGPT for their main search on day one

**70%** are named within 90 days

**5 to 10 in 100** new customers say they found the business through AI

## How many businesses AI names

**73%**

73% of the 128,400+ local businesses Local AI Registry has scored are named by zero AI assistants (our estimate from AI-visibility checks).

Source: [Local AI Registry data](../methodology/index.html)

**85.6%**

In a census of every venue in two markets, 85.6% were never recommended by any of four assistants. Being named was associated with having a website, more reviews, listed prices and web mentions (Pitenin 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**3.5%**

Only 3.5% of businesses ChatGPT named in localized searches appeared at every test point across a town (BrightLocal, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**1 in 75**

Across the businesses we've scored, nearly two in three land below 45 out of 100 on the AI Score, and barely one in seventy-five clears 65.

Source: [What is an AI Score?](../journal/what-is-an-ai-score/index.html)

## Where AI gets its answers

**76.4%**

Local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, compared with 13.7% of all searches.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**67.5%**

News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google's AI answers about local businesses.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**6.5%**

Businesses' own websites supplied just 6.5% of those citations.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**70 of 147**

Brand websites ranked on page one for 147 of 157 brand questions, but AI cited them in only 70.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**0.737**

In a 75,000-brand study, the top correlate of AI visibility was YouTube and branded web mentions (0.737), not links or pages (Ahrefs, cited in our white paper The Convergence).

Source: [The Convergence](../proof/the-convergence-white-paper/index.html)

**51.6%**

For claims AI attributed to a store locator, app or official site, 51.6% were not supported by any page it cited.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**78%**

Cited social posts had a median of 8 readable words, and 78% were too thin to verify anything.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

## How AI answers change

**29%**

When ChatGPT got the same local question about 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses it named appeared in both answers (8ight.AI, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**0.46**

Asked the same query twice, Google Search shared 0.78 of its sources, AI Overviews 0.66 and Gemini 0.46 (Grossman et al., SIGIR 2026, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**two-thirds**

Rewording the same local question changed about two-thirds of the sources Google's AI cited.

Source: [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-001

**100 answers**

For a business named in 40% of answers, the likely range is roughly 17% to 69% after 10 answers, and 31% to 50% after 100 (our calculation).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

From our data · 3D

## Local searches vs question searches

## Healthcare and specialists

**74.7%**

Asking for "an oculoplastic surgeon" returned specialists 74.7% of the time, compared with 46.6% for "a doctor who does eyelid lifts" (Parikh et al., 2024, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**63.9%**

Doctors named by AI matched real clinicians 63.9% of the time with web search, compared with 10.8% without it (Ibrahim and Zaki, 2026, preprint, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

**52.8%**

ChatGPT declined to recommend an orthopedic surgeon in 52.8% of 40,500 persona-based requests (Haupt et al., 2026, reviewed in our brief).

Source: [How Often AI Recommends Your Business](../research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html) · LAIR-R-2026-002

## What does the research say?

From [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html), our study of how Google's AI answers local business questions. Every number links to its chart.

**Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average.Figure 3, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**Who Google’s AI cites for local business questions vs everything else.** In local answers, Gannett newspapers supplied 28.3% of citations and appeared in 90.3% of answers. Businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5% of citations.Figure 5, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap.png)

**Ranked on page one, skipped by the AI: brand websites in local answers.** Brand websites appeared on page one in 147 of 157 brand questions but were cited in 70. Walmart ranked in 11 of 15 answers and was cited once.Figure 10, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/brand-website-ranked-vs-cited-google-ai-overviews.png)

**173 of 207 local AI answers told people to check with their local store.** 83.6% of local AI answers sent the reader back to the store (“check your local store,” “call ahead,” “hours may vary”), against 2.6% of other answers.Figure 14, [The Local Answer Gap](../research/local-answer-gap/index.html#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle), Local AI Registry Research, 2026 · [SVG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.svg) · [PNG](../research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.png)

# Trust and Integrity

> Local AI Registry keeps the public record of what AI says about local business. The method is open, rank is never for sale, and you control your own entry.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/trust/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Trust

Trust & integrity

## A record is only worth the standards behind it.

We keep the public record of what AI says about local business. That only means something if the method is open, the rankings are never for sale, and you can see and control your own entry. Here is how we hold that line.

What we hold ourselves to

## The standards.

01

### The method is public

Eight signals, one number, every weight written down. You can read exactly how a score is built, line by line, on the methodology page.

02

### We never sell rank

No business can buy a higher score or a softer write-up, and no one can pay to be removed from a rival’s list. Independence is the whole point of a record.

03

### Your entry, your control

See what we hold about your business, correct anything wrong, or remove yourself from the register. The controls are below, and they’re free.

04

### We fix mistakes

Flag anything inaccurate and a real person reviews it, usually within two business days. A public record has to be a correct one.

05

### We don’t manufacture certainty

When the data is thin, we say so rather than inventing a number. A score you can’t trust is worse than no score at all.

Editorial independence

# Trust center

> How Local AI Registry protects your business and your customers: HIPAA BAA, 256-bit encryption, $750K insurance, approvals and the rules we never break.

Source: https://localairegistry.com/trust-center/
Updated: 2026-11-15
Publisher: Local AI Registry (https://localairegistry.com)

Security and privacy

How we protect your business, your customers' privacy and the integrity of the Registry.

**HIPAA ready** We sign a BAA with every healthcare practice. Sign it online in two minutes.

**Bank-level security** 256-bit encryption on Google Cloud. Your data stays yours.

**$750K insured** Professional liability and cyber coverage, so you're protected.

**Irvine, California HQ** US-headquartered, with experts around the world.

**Replies within 24 hours** A real person, not a ticket queue.

**Month to month** No long-term contracts. Stay because it works.

**You review everything** Every reply, post and article goes to you for review first.

**Your area is yours** We don't take on a business like yours in your area. We agree on the exact area with you before we start.

## By the numbers

The track record behind the promises on this page.

**10+** years helping local businesses get found

**85%** of clients stay past year one

**4.9★** from 25 Google reviews

**5** press stories about our work

## Things we will never do

- A business can't buy a better score.
- A specialist can't buy a better track record.
- Private customer information doesn't become public because it might be useful to AI.
- Our own services sit in the same list, under the same rules, with no boost.

## The guardrails built into the work

Trust isn't a badge. It's what the system refuses to do. These rules run on every account:

- **No medical claims.** A scan runs on every draft and on the title. An outcome promise, a recovery time, a typical result or a safety word blocks the draft outright for health-adjacent categories.
- **No described before and after photos.** A photo classified as a result is never described and never published by us. Advertising rules on outcome claims apply to a picture the same way they apply to a sentence.
- **Bad reviews wait for you.** Only if you approve one. A one or two star review is read by our team first, and where a reply is written it is held until it reaches you, so nothing goes up under your name unless you approve it.
- **Press releases wait for your yes.** A press release never goes out unless you approve it. If the deadline passes without you sending it, we cancel the order, tell you we did not buy it, and draft a fresh one on the next round.
- **Nothing buys itself.** Queued, never auto-confirmed. A person on our team confirms every purchase, under a spending limit, so nothing buys itself.
- **A failed check is recorded as a failure.** We record the answer text, the businesses named in it, and where you came in. If a check fails, we record it as a failed check, never as you not being named.
- **A person reads your report first.** Yes. Three days before your date it goes to your assigned expert and two people here as a preview, and it can be corrected or held in that window.

## Frequently asked questions

Do you replace my agency?

You can, or we can work alongside them. If a studio runs your website, keep them. We handle the AI visibility work across the other signals and report on it.

Why is one team cheaper than nine vendors?

Because the work overlaps. One verified record feeds your listings, your Google profile, your press and your website, so nothing is written twice.

What if my agency already does SEO?

SEO is part of it, and a good foundation. AI answers also lean on reviews, press, best-of lists and outside articles. We cover all of them.
